व्रतं त्रिरात्रमुद्दिश्य दिवारात्रं स्थिता'ऽश्रमे .. 46 ..
16.166.m: Thinking, ‘He must die on the fourth day,’ that splendid woman, / undertaking a three-night vow, stayed day and night in the hermitage.

16.166.s:
tatastrirātraṃ nyavasatsnātvā saṃtarpya devatām ..
śvaśrūśvaśurayoḥ pādau vavaṃde cāruhāsinī .. 47 ..
16.166.d:
ततस्त्रिरात्रं न्यवसत्स्नात्वा संतर्प्य देवताम् ..
श्वश्रूश्वशुरयोः पादौ ववंदे चारुहासिनी .. 47 ..
16.166.m: Then, having observed the three nights, having bathed and propitiated the deity, / she of charming smile bowed down at the feet of her mother-in-law and father-in-law.

16.166.s:
atha pratasthe paraśuṃ gṛhītvā satyavānvanam ..
sāvitryapi ca bhartāraṃ gacchaṃtaṃ pṛṣṭhato'nvayāt .. 48 ..
16.166.d:
अथ प्रतस्थे परशुं गृहीत्वा सत्यवान्वनम् ..
सावित्र्यपि च भर्तारं गच्छंतं पृष्ठतोऽन्वयात् .. 48 ..
16.166.m: Then Satyavān set out for the forest, taking an axe; / Sāvitrī also followed behind her departing husband.

16.166.s:
tato gṛhītvā tarasā phalapuṣpasamitkuśān ..
atha śuṣkāṇi cādāya kāṣṭhabhāramakalpayat .. 49 ..
16.166.d:
ततो गृहीत्वा तरसा फलपुष्पसमित्कुशान् ..
अथ शुष्काणि चादाय काष्ठभारमकल्पयत् .. 49 ..
16.166.m: Then, having quickly gathered fruits, flowers, kindling, and kuśa grass, / and taking dry firewood, he prepared a load of wood.

16.166.s:
atha pāṭayataḥ kāṣṭhaṃ jātā śirasi vedanā ..
kāṣṭhabhāraṃ kṣaṇāttyaktvā vaṭaśākhāvalaṃbitaḥ .. 7.1.166.50 ..
16.166.d:
अथ पाटयतः काष्ठं जाता शिरसि वेदना ..
काष्ठभारं क्षणात्त्यक्त्वा वटशाखावलंबितः .. 7.1.166.50 ..
16.166.m: Then, as he was splitting the wood, a pain arose in his head; / letting go of the load of wood in an instant, clinging to a banyan branch,

16.166.s:
sāvitrīṃ prāha śiraso vedanā māṃ prabādhate ..
tavotsaṃge kṣaṇaṃ tāvatsvaptumicchāmi sundari .. 51 ..
16.166.d:
सावित्रीं प्राह शिरसो वेदना मां प्रबाधते ..
तवोत्संगे क्षणं तावत्स्वप्तुमिच्छामि सुन्दरि .. 51 ..
16.166.m: he said to Sāvitrī: “A pain in my head torments me; / I wish to sleep for a moment on your lap, O lovely one.”

16.166.s:
viśramasva mahābāho sāvitrī prāha duḥkhitā ..
paścādapi gamiṣyāmi hyāśramaṃ śramanāśanam .. .. 52 ..
16.166.d:
विश्रमस्व महाबाहो सावित्री प्राह दुःखिता ..
पश्चादपि गमिष्यामि ह्याश्रमं श्रमनाशनम् .. .. 52 ..
16.166.m: “Rest, O mighty-armed one,” Sāvitrī said sorrowfully; / “afterwards we shall go to the hermitage that removes fatigue.”

16.166.s:
yāvadutsaṃgagaṃ kṛtvā śirosya tu mahītale ..
tāvaddadarśa sāvitrī puruṣaṃ kṛṣṇapiṃgalam .. 53 ..
16.166.d:
यावदुत्संगगं कृत्वा शिरोस्य तु महीतले ..
तावद्ददर्श सावित्री पुरुषं कृष्णपिंगलम् .. 53 ..
16.166.m: As she placed his head upon her lap on the surface of the earth, / just then Sāvitrī saw a dark and tawny man,

16.166.s:
kirīṭinaṃ pītavastraṃ sākṣātsūryamivoditam ..
tamuvācātha sāvitrī praṇamya madhurākṣaram .. 54 ..
16.166.d:
किरीटिनं पीतवस्त्रं साक्षात्सूर्यमिवोदितम् ..
तमुवाचाथ सावित्री प्रणम्य मधुराक्षरम् .. 54 ..
16.166.m: wearing a diadem, dressed in yellow garments, like the risen sun itself. / Then Sāvitrī bowed down and spoke to him in sweet words:

16.166.s:
kastvaṃ devo'thavā daityo yo māṃ dharṣitumāgataḥ ..
na cāhaṃ kenacicchakyā svadharmāddeva rodhitum .. 55 ..
16.166.d:
कस्त्वं देवोऽथवा दैत्यो यो मां धर्षितुमागतः ..
न चाहं केनचिच्छक्या स्वधर्माद्देव रोधितुम् .. 55 ..
16.166.m: “Who are you—a god or a Daitya—who has come to assail me? / And I cannot be deflected from my own duty by anyone, O divine one.

16.166.s: viddhi māṃ puruṣaśreṣṭha dīptāmagniśikhāmiva .. 56 ..
16.166.d: विद्धि मां पुरुषश्रेष्ठ दीप्तामग्निशिखामिव .. 56 ..
16.166.m: Know me, O best of men, to be like a blazing flame of fire.”

16.166.s:
.. yama uvāca .. ..
yamaḥ saṃyamanaścāsmi sarvalokabhayaṃkaraḥ .. 57 ..
16.166.d:
.. यम उवाच .. ..
यमः संयमनश्चास्मि सर्वलोकभयंकरः .. 57 ..
16.166.m: Yama said: / “I am Yama the Restrainer, who inspires fear in all the worlds.

16.166.s:
kṣīṇāyureṣa te bhartā saṃnidhau te pativrate ..
na śakyaḥ kiṃkarairnetumato'haṃ svayamāgataḥ .. 58 ..
16.166.d:
क्षीणायुरेष ते भर्ता संनिधौ ते पतिव्रते ..
न शक्यः किंकरैर्नेतुमतोऽहं स्वयमागतः .. 58 ..
16.166.m: Your husband’s lifespan is exhausted; while he is in your presence, O devoted wife, / my attendants cannot lead him away; therefore I have come in person.”

16.166.s:
evamuktvā satyavrataśarīrātpāśasaṃyutaḥ ..
aṃguṣṭhamātraṃ puruṣaṃ nicakarṣa yamo balāt .. 59 ..
16.166.d:
एवमुक्त्वा सत्यव्रतशरीरात्पाशसंयुतः ..
अंगुष्ठमात्रं पुरुषं निचकर्ष यमो बलात् .. 59 ..
16.166.m: Having spoken thus, holding a noose, Yama pulled out by force / from Satyavrata’s body a man the size of a thumb.

16.166.s:
atha prayātumārebhe paṃthānaṃ pitṛsevitam ..
sāvitryapi varārohā pṛṣṭhato'nujagāma ha .. 7.1.166.60 ..
16.166.d:
अथ प्रयातुमारेभे पंथानं पितृसेवितम् ..
सावित्र्यपि वरारोहा पृष्ठतोऽनुजगाम ह .. 7.1.166.60 ..
16.166.m: Then he began to travel upon the path frequented by the ancestors; / Sāvitrī, too, of shapely hips, followed behind him.

16.166.s:
pativratatvāccāśrāṃtā tāmuvāca yamastathā ..
nivarta gaccha sāvitri muhūrtaṃ tvamihāgatā .. 61 ..
16.166.d:
पतिव्रतत्वाच्चाश्रांता तामुवाच यमस्तथा ..
निवर्त गच्छ सावित्रि मुहूर्तं त्वमिहागता .. 61 ..
16.166.m: Untired on account of her devotion to her husband, Yama spoke to her thus: / “Turn back, go, O Sāvitrī; you have come this far for a moment.

16.166.s: eṣa mārgo viśālākṣi na kenāpyanugamyate .. 62 ..
16.166.d: एष मार्गो विशालाक्षि न केनाप्यनुगम्यते .. 62 ..
16.166.m: This path, O large-eyed one, is not to be followed by anyone.”

16.166.s:
.. sāvitryuvāca .. ..
na śramo na ca me glāniḥ kadācidapi jāyate ..
bhartāramanugacchantyā viśiṣṭasya ca saṃnidhau .. 63 ..
16.166.d:
.. सावित्र्युवाच .. ..
न श्रमो न च मे ग्लानिः कदाचिदपि जायते ..
भर्तारमनुगच्छन्त्या विशिष्टस्य च संनिधौ .. 63 ..
16.166.m: Sāvitrī said: / “No weariness and no exhaustion ever arises in me / as I follow my husband, and in the presence of an exalted one.

16.166.s:
satāṃ santo gatirnānyā strīṇāṃ bhartā sadā gatiḥ ..
vedo varṇāśramāṇāṃ ca śiṣyāṇāṃ ca gatirguruḥ .. 64 ..
16.166.d:
सतां सन्तो गतिर्नान्या स्त्रीणां भर्ता सदा गतिः ..
वेदो वर्णाश्रमाणां च शिष्याणां च गतिर्गुरुः .. 64 ..
16.166.m: The good are the refuge of the good, no other; a husband is always the refuge of women; / the Veda is the refuge of the classes and life-stages, and the teacher is the refuge of disciples.

16.166.s:
sarveṣāmeva bhūtānāṃ sthānamasti mahītale ..
bharttāramekamutsṛjya strīṇāṃ nānyaḥ samāśrayaḥ .. 65 ..
16.166.d:
सर्वेषामेव भूतानां स्थानमस्ति महीतले ..
भर्त्तारमेकमुत्सृज्य स्त्रीणां नान्यः समाश्रयः .. 65 ..
16.166.m: For all beings there is a place on the surface of the earth; / women have no refuge other than their husband alone.”

16.166.s:
evamanyaiḥ sumadhurairvākyairdharmārthasaṃhitaiḥ ..
tutoṣa sūryatanayaḥ sāvitrīṃ vākyamabravīt .. 66 ..
16.166.d:
एवमन्यैः सुमधुरैर्वाक्यैर्धर्मार्थसंहितैः ..
तुतोष सूर्यतनयः सावित्रीं वाक्यमब्रवीत् .. 66 ..
16.166.m: With other such very sweet words endowed with righteousness and meaning, / the son of the Sun was pleased, and he addressed Sāvitrī:

16.166.s:
.. yama uvāca .. ..
tuṣṭo'smi tava bhadraṃ te varaṃ varaya bhāmini ..
sāpi vavre ca rājyaṃ svaṃ vinayāvanatānanā .. 67 ..
16.166.d:
.. यम उवाच .. ..
तुष्टोऽस्मि तव भद्रं ते वरं वरय भामिनि ..
सापि वव्रे च राज्यं स्वं विनयावनतानना .. 67 ..
16.166.m: Yama said: / “I am pleased with you, good fortune to you! Choose a boon, O beautiful woman.” / With her face bowed in modesty, she chose their kingdom,

16.166.s:
cakṣuḥprāptiṃ tathā rājyaṃ śvaśurasya mahātmanaḥ ..
pituḥ putraśataṃ caiva putrāṇāṃ śatamātmanaḥ .. 68 ..
16.166.d:
चक्षुःप्राप्तिं तथा राज्यं श्वशुरस्य महात्मनः ..
पितुः पुत्रशतं चैव पुत्राणां शतमात्मनः .. 68 ..
16.166.m: the restoration of eyesight and the kingdom for her noble father-in-law, / a hundred sons for her father, and a hundred sons for herself,

16.166.s:
jīvitaṃ ca tathā bharturdharmasiddhiṃ ca śāśvatīm ..
dharmarājo varaṃ dattvā preṣayāmāsa tāṃ tataḥ .. 69 ..
16.166.d:
जीवितं च तथा भर्तुर्धर्मसिद्धिं च शाश्वतीम् ..
धर्मराजो वरं दत्त्वा प्रेषयामास तां ततः .. 69 ..
16.166.m: and the life of her husband, and eternal attainment of dharma. / Having granted the boons, the King of Dharma then sent her away.

16.166.s:
atha bhartāramāsādya sāvitrī hṛṣṭamānasā ..
jagāma svāśramapadaṃ saha bhartrā nirākulā .. 7.1.166.70 ..
16.166.d:
अथ भर्तारमासाद्य सावित्री हृष्टमानसा ..
जगाम स्वाश्रमपदं सह भर्त्रा निराकुला .. 7.1.166.70 ..
16.166.m: Then, having reached her husband, Sāvitrī, glad at heart, / went untroubled to her own hermitage together with her husband.

16.166.s:
jyeṣṭhasya pūrṇimāyāṃ ca tayā cīrṇaṃ vrataṃ tvidam ..
māhātmyato'sya nṛpateścakṣuḥprāptirabhūtpuraḥ .. 71 ..
16.166.d:
ज्येष्ठस्य पूर्णिमायां च तया चीर्णं व्रतं त्विदम् ..
माहात्म्यतोऽस्य नृपतेश्चक्षुःप्राप्तिरभूत्पुरः .. 71 ..
16.166.m: And on the full moon of Jyeṣṭha, this observance was performed by her. / Through its māhātmya, the king first regained his eyesight.

16.166.s:
tataḥ svadeśarājyaṃ ca prāpa niṣkaṇṭakaṃ nṛpaḥ ..
pitāsyāḥ putraśatakaṃ sā ca lebhe sutāñchatam .. 72 ..
16.166.d:
ततः स्वदेशराज्यं च प्राप निष्कण्टकं नृपः ..
पितास्याः पुत्रशतकं सा च लेभे सुताञ्छतम् .. 72 ..
16.166.m: Then the king obtained his own realm free from thorns. / Her father obtained a hundred sons, and she obtained a hundred sons.

16.166.s: evaṃ vratasya māhātmyaṃ kathitaṃ sakalaṃ mayā .. 73 .. ..
16.166.d: एवं व्रतस्य माहात्म्यं कथितं सकलं मया .. 73 .. ..
16.166.m: Thus the entire māhātmya of the observance has been recounted by me.

16.166.s:
.. devyuvāca .. ..
kīdṛśaṃ tadvrataṃ deva sāvitryā caritaṃ mahat ..
tasmiṃstu jyeṣṭhamāse hi vidhānaṃ tasya kīdṛśam .. 74 ..
16.166.d:
.. देव्युवाच .. ..
कीदृशं तद्व्रतं देव सावित्र्या चरितं महत् ..
तस्मिंस्तु ज्येष्ठमासे हि विधानं तस्य कीदृशम् .. 74 ..
16.166.m: The Devī said: / Of what kind was that great observance, O Lord, performed by Sāvitrī / in that month of Jyeṣṭha, and what is its rite?

16.166.s:
kā devatā vrate tasminke mantrāḥ kiṃ phalaṃ vibho ..
vistareṇa maheśa tvaṃ brūhi dharmaṃ sanātanam .. 76 ..
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
śrūyatāṃ devadeveśi sāvitrīvratamā darāt ..
kathayāmi yathā cīrṇaṃ tayā satyā maheśvari .. 76 ..
16.166.d:
का देवता व्रते तस्मिन्के मन्त्राः किं फलं विभो ..
विस्तरेण महेश त्वं ब्रूहि धर्मं सनातनम् .. 76 ..
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
श्रूयतां देवदेवेशि सावित्रीव्रतमा दरात् ..
कथयामि यथा चीर्णं तया सत्या महेश्वरि .. 76 ..
16.166.m:
Who is the deity in that observance? What are the mantras? What is the fruit, O All-pervading One? / Tell in detail, O Maheśa, the eternal dharma.
Īśvara said: / Listen with devotion, O queen of the god of gods, to the Sāvitrī observance, / O Maheśvarī; I shall recount how it was performed by that faithful woman.

16.166.s:
trayodaśyāṃ tu jyeṣṭhasya dantadhāvanapūrvakam ..
trirātraṃ niyamaṃ kuryādupavāsasya bhāmini .. 77 ..
16.166.d:
त्रयोदश्यां तु ज्येष्ठस्य दन्तधावनपूर्वकम् ..
त्रिरात्रं नियमं कुर्यादुपवासस्य भामिनि .. 77 ..
16.166.m: On the thirteenth day of Jyeṣṭha, preceded by cleaning the teeth, / one should undertake a three-night rule of fasting, O passionate lady.

16.166.s:
aśaktastu trayodaśyāṃ naktaṃ kuryājjitendriyaḥ ..
ayācitaṃ caturdaśyāṃ hyupavāsena pūrṇimām .. 78 ..
16.166.d:
अशक्तस्तु त्रयोदश्यां नक्तं कुर्याज्जितेन्द्रियः ..
अयाचितं चतुर्दश्यां ह्युपवासेन पूर्णिमाम् .. 78 ..
16.166.m: One who is unable, having subdued the senses, should observe a night meal on the thirteenth, / unsolicited food on the fourteenth, and the full moon with a complete fast.

16.166.s:
nityaṃ snātvā taḍāge vā mahānadyāṃ ca nirjhare ..
pāṃḍukūpe tu suśroṇi sarvasnānaphalaṃ labhet .. 79 ..
16.166.d:
नित्यं स्नात्वा तडागे वा महानद्यां च निर्झरे ..
पांडुकूपे तु सुश्रोणि सर्वस्नानफलं लभेत् .. 79 ..
16.166.m: Having constantly bathed in a pond, a great river, or a torrent, / one obtains the fruit of all ritual ablutions at the Pāṇḍukūpa, O woman of beautiful hips.

16.166.s: viśeṣātpūrṇimāyāṃ tu snānaṃ sarṣapamṛjjalaiḥ .. 7.1.166.80 ..
16.166.m: Especially on the full moon, there is a ritual ablution with water mixed with mustard and clay.

16.166.s:
gṛhītvā vālukaṃ pātre prasthamātre yaśasvini ..
athavā dhānyamādāya yavaśālitilādikam .. 81 ..
16.166.d:
गृहीत्वा वालुकं पात्रे प्रस्थमात्रे यशस्विनि ..
अथवा धान्यमादाय यवशालितिलादिकम् .. 81 ..
16.166.m: Having taken sand in a vessel measuring a prastha, O illustrious lady, / or having taken grain—barley, rice, sesame, and the rest,

16.166.s:
tato vaṃśamaye pātre vastrayugmena veṣṭite ..
sāvitrīpratimāṃ kṛtvā sarvāvayavaśobhitām.. 82 ..
16.166.d:
ततो वंशमये पात्रे वस्त्रयुग्मेन वेष्टिते ..
सावित्रीप्रतिमां कृत्वा सर्वावयवशोभिताम्.. 82 ..
16.166.m: then, having fashioned in a bamboo vessel wrapped with a pair of cloths / an image of Sāvitrī adorned with all limbs,

16.166.s:
sauvarṇīṃ mṛnmayīṃ vāpi svaśaktyā dārunirmitām ..
raktavastradvayaṃ dadyātsāvitryā brahmaṇaḥ sitam .. 83 ..
16.166.d:
सौवर्णीं मृन्मयीं वापि स्वशक्त्या दारुनिर्मिताम् ..
रक्तवस्त्रद्वयं दद्यात्सावित्र्या ब्रह्मणः सितम् .. 83 ..
16.166.m: made of gold or of clay, or made of wood according to one's means, / one should give a pair of red garments to Sāvitrī, and a white one to Brahmā.

16.166.s:
sāvitrīṃ brahmaṇā sārdhamevaṃ śaktyā prapūjayet ..
gandhaiḥ sugandhapuṣpaiśca dhūpanaivedyadīpakaiḥ .. 94 ..
pūrṇakośātakaiḥ pakvaiḥ kūṣmāṇḍakarkaṭīphalaiḥ ..
nālikeraiḥ sakharjūraiḥ kapitthairdāḍimaiḥ śubhaiḥ .. 85 ..
jaṃbūjaṃbīranāriṃgairakṣoṭaiḥ panasaistathā ..
jīrakaiḥ kaṭukhaṇḍaiśca guḍena lavaṇena ca .. 86 ..
virūḍhaiḥ saptadhānyaiśca vaṃśapātraprakalpitaiḥ ..
raṃjayetpaṭṭasūtraiśca śubhaiḥ kuṃkumakesaraiḥ .. 87 ..
avatāraṃ karotyevaṃ sāvitrī brahmaṇaḥ priyā .. 88 ..
tāmarccayīta mantreṇa sāvitryā brahmaṇā samam..
itareṣāṃ purāṇokto maṃtro'yaṃ samudāhṛtaḥ .. 89 ..
oṃkārapūrvake devi vīṇāpustakadhāriṇi ..
vedāṃbike namastubhyamavaidhavyaṃ prayaccha me ..7.1.166.90..
16.166.d:
सावित्रीं ब्रह्मणा सार्धमेवं शक्त्या प्रपूजयेत् ..
गन्धैः सुगन्धपुष्पैश्च धूपनैवेद्यदीपकैः .. 94 ..
पूर्णकोशातकैः पक्वैः कूष्माण्डकर्कटीफलैः ..
नालिकेरैः सखर्जूरैः कपित्थैर्दाडिमैः शुभैः .. 85 ..
जंबूजंबीरनारिंगैरक्षोटैः पनसैस्तथा ..
जीरकैः कटुखण्डैश्च गुडेन लवणेन च .. 86 ..
विरूढैः सप्तधान्यैश्च वंशपात्रप्रकल्पितैः ..
रंजयेत्पट्टसूत्रैश्च शुभैः कुंकुमकेसरैः .. 87 ..
अवतारं करोत्येवं सावित्री ब्रह्मणः प्रिया .. 88 ..
तामर्च्चयीत मन्त्रेण सावित्र्या ब्रह्मणा समम्..
इतरेषां पुराणोक्तो मंत्रोऽयं समुदाहृतः .. 89 ..
ओंकारपूर्वके देवि वीणापुस्तकधारिणि ..
वेदांबिके नमस्तुभ्यमवैधव्यं प्रयच्छ मे ..7.1.166.90..
16.166.m:
Thus, according to one's capacity, one should worship Sāvitrī together with Brahmā / with perfumes, fragrant flowers, incense, food offerings, and lamps,
with ripe full loofahs, gourds, and cucumbers, / with coconuts, dates, wood apples, and auspicious pomegranates,
with rose apples, citrons, oranges, walnuts, and jackfruits, / with cumin, pieces of bitter spices, molasses, and salt,
and with the sprouted seven grains arranged in a bamboo vessel; / and one should colour it with silk threads and auspicious saffron filaments.
Thus Sāvitrī, the beloved of Brahmā, descends.
One should worship her together with Brahmā with the Sāvitrī mantra. / For the others, this mantra proclaimed in the Purāṇa is recited:
‘O goddess preceded by the syllable Om, holding a vīṇā and a book, / O mother of the Vedas, salutations to you! Grant me freedom from widowhood!’

16.166.s:
evaṃ saṃpūjya vidhivajjāgaraṃ tatra kārayet..
gītavāditraśabdenanaranārīkadaṃbakam ..
nṛtyaddhasannayedrātriṃ nṛtyaśāstraviśāradaiḥ .. 91 ..
sāvitryākhyānakaṃ cāpi vācayīta dvijottamān..
yāvatprabhātasamayaṃ gītabhāvarasaiḥ saha .. 92 ..
vivāhamevaṃ kṛtvā tu sāvitryā brahmaṇā saha ..
paridhāpya sitairvastrairdaṃpatīnāṃ tu saptakam .. 93 ..
gṛhadānaṃ pradātavyaṃ sarvopaskarasaṃyutam ..
brāhmaṇe vedaviduṣe sāvitrīṃ vinivedayet .. 94 ..
16.166.d:
एवं संपूज्य विधिवज्जागरं तत्र कारयेत्..
गीतवादित्रशब्देननरनारीकदंबकम् ..
नृत्यद्धसन्नयेद्रात्रिं नृत्यशास्त्रविशारदैः .. 91 ..
सावित्र्याख्यानकं चापि वाचयीत द्विजोत्तमान्..
यावत्प्रभातसमयं गीतभावरसैः सह .. 92 ..
विवाहमेवं कृत्वा तु सावित्र्या ब्रह्मणा सह ..
परिधाप्य सितैर्वस्त्रैर्दंपतीनां तु सप्तकम् .. 93 ..
गृहदानं प्रदातव्यं सर्वोपस्करसंयुतम् ..
ब्राह्मणे वेदविदुषे सावित्रीं विनिवेदयेत् .. 94 ..
16.166.m:
Having worshipped thus according to rule, one should keep a vigil there. / With the sound of singing and musical instruments, a crowd of men and women, / dancing and laughing, should spend the night with those skilled in the science of dance.
And one should have the best of twice-born recite the tale of Sāvitrī / until daybreak, along with the rasas of song and sentiment.
Having performed in this manner the marriage of Sāvitrī with Brahmā, / and having clothed seven married couples in white garments,
a gift of a house should be given, accompanied by all utensils. / One should present the Sāvitrī [image] to a brahmin learned in the Veda,

16.166.s:
atha sāvitrīkalpajñe sāvitryākhyānavācake ..
daivajñe hyuñchavṛttisthe daridre cāgnihotriṇi .. 95 ..
16.166.d:
अथ सावित्रीकल्पज्ञे सावित्र्याख्यानवाचके ..
दैवज्ञे ह्युञ्छवृत्तिस्थे दरिद्रे चाग्निहोत्रिणि .. 95 ..
16.166.m: or to one who knows the ritual of Sāvitrī, a reciter of the tale of Sāvitrī, / an astrologer, one who lives by gleaning, or a poor agnihotrin.

16.166.s:
evaṃ dattvā vidhānena tasyāṃ rātrau nimantrayet ..
paurṇamāsyāṃ vaṭādhastāddaṃpatīnāṃ caturdaśa .. 96 ..
16.166.d:
एवं दत्त्वा विधानेन तस्यां रात्रौ निमन्त्रयेत् ..
पौर्णमास्यां वटाधस्ताद्दंपतीनां चतुर्दश .. 96 ..
16.166.m: Having given in this manner according to the rite, one should invite on that night / fourteen married couples under a banyan tree on the full moon.

16.166.s:
tataḥ prabhātasamaye uṣaḥkāla upasthite ..
bhakṣyabhojyādikaṃ sarvaṃ sāvitrīsthalamānayet .. 97..
16.166.d:
ततः प्रभातसमये उषःकाल उपस्थिते ..
भक्ष्यभोज्यादिकं सर्वं सावित्रीस्थलमानयेत् .. 97..
16.166.m: Then at dawn, when daybreak has arrived, / one should bring all chewable and edible food to the site of Sāvitrī.

16.166.s:
pākaṃ kṛtvā tu śucinā rakṣāṃ kṛtvā prayatnataḥ ..
brāhmaṇāngṛhiṇīyuktāṃstata āhvānayetsudhīḥ .. 98 ..
16.166.d:
पाकं कृत्वा तु शुचिना रक्षां कृत्वा प्रयत्नतः ..
ब्राह्मणान्गृहिणीयुक्तांस्तत आह्वानयेत्सुधीः .. 98 ..
16.166.m: Having cooked with purity and having guarded [it] with care, / the wise person should then summon the brahmins accompanied by their wives.

16.166.s:
sāvitryāḥ sthalake tatra kṛtvā pādābhiṣecanam ..
susnātānbrāhmaṇāṃstatra sabhāryānupaveśayet .. 99 ..
16.166.d:
सावित्र्याः स्थलके तत्र कृत्वा पादाभिषेचनम् ..
सुस्नातान्ब्राह्मणांस्तत्र सभार्यानुपवेशयेत् .. 99 ..
16.166.m: Having performed the washing of their feet there at the site of Sāvitrī, / one should seat the well-bathed brahmins there along with their wives.

16.166.s:
sāvitryāḥ purato devi daṃpatyorbhojanaṃ dadet ..
tenāhaṃ bhojitastatra bhavāmīha na saṃśaya .. 7.1.166.100 ..
16.166.d:
सावित्र्याः पुरतो देवि दंपत्योर्भोजनं ददेत् ..
तेनाहं भोजितस्तत्र भवामीह न संशय .. 7.1.166.100 ..
16.166.m: In front of Sāvitrī, O Devī, one should offer a meal to the married couples. / By that, I am fed there in this world; there is no doubt.

16.166.s:
dvitīyaṃ bhojayedyastu bhojitastena keśavaḥ ..
lakṣmyāḥ sahāyo varado varāṃstasya prayacchati .. 101 ..
16.166.d:
द्वितीयं भोजयेद्यस्तु भोजितस्तेन केशवः ..
लक्ष्म्याः सहायो वरदो वरांस्तस्य प्रयच्छति .. 101 ..
16.166.m: He who feeds a second [couple] feeds Keśava. / The companion of Lakṣmī, the giver of boons, bestows boons upon him.

16.166.s:
sāvitryā sahito brahmā tṛtīye bhojito bhavet ..
ekaikaṃ bhojanaṃ tatra koṭibhojasamaṃ smṛtam .. 102 ..
16.166.d:
सावित्र्या सहितो ब्रह्मा तृतीये भोजितो भवेत् ..
एकैकं भोजनं तत्र कोटिभोजसमं स्मृतम् .. 102 ..
16.166.m: Brahmā accompanied by Sāvitrī becomes fed in the third. / Each single meal there is declared equal to ten million meals.

16.166.s:
aṣṭādaśaprakāreṇa ṣaḍrasīkṛtabhojanam ..
devyāstatra mahādevi sāvitrīsthalasannidhau .. 103 ..
16.166.d:
अष्टादशप्रकारेण षड्रसीकृतभोजनम् ..
देव्यास्तत्र महादेवि सावित्रीस्थलसन्निधौ .. 103 ..
16.166.m: A meal of eighteen varieties seasoned with the six tastes / [is offered] to the Devī there, O Mahādevī, in the presence of Sāvitrī’s site.

16.166.s:
vidhavā na kule tasya na vaṃdhyā na ca durbhagā ..
na kanyājananī cāpi na ca syādbharturapriyā ..
aṣṭau doṣāstu nārīṇāṃ na bhavaṃti kadācana .. 104 ..
16.166.d:
विधवा न कुले तस्य न वंध्या न च दुर्भगा ..
न कन्याजननी चापि न च स्याद्भर्तुरप्रिया ..
अष्टौ दोषास्तु नारीणां न भवंति कदाचन .. 104 ..
16.166.m: In his family there is no widow, no barren woman, and no unfortunate woman, / nor one who bears only daughters, nor one disliked by her husband. / The eight faults of women never occur.

16.166.s:
tasmātsarvaprayatnena sāvitryagre ca bhojanam ..
dātavyaṃ sarvadā devi kaṭunīlavivarjitam .. 105 ..
16.166.d:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन सावित्र्यग्रे च भोजनम् ..
दातव्यं सर्वदा देवि कटुनीलविवर्जितम् .. 105 ..
16.166.m: Therefore, with every effort, in front of Sāvitrī a meal / should always be given, O Devī, devoid of pungent and indigo foods.

16.166.s:
na cāmlaṃ na ca vai kṣāraṃ strīṇāṃ bhojyaṃ kadācana ..
paṃcaprakāraṃ madhuraṃ hṛdyaṃ sarvaṃ susaṃskṛtam .. 106 ..
16.166.d:
न चाम्लं न च वै क्षारं स्त्रीणां भोज्यं कदाचन ..
पंचप्रकारं मधुरं हृद्यं सर्वं सुसंस्कृतम् .. 106 ..
16.166.m: Neither sour nor alkaline food is ever to be eaten by women; / it should be of five kinds, sweet, agreeable, and all well prepared.

16.166.s:
ghṛtapūrṇāpūpakāśca bahukṣīrasamanvitāḥ ..
pūpakāstādṛśāḥ kāryā dvitīyā'śokavartikā .. 107 ..
16.166.d:
घृतपूर्णापूपकाश्च बहुक्षीरसमन्विताः ..
पूपकास्तादृशाः कार्या द्वितीयाऽशोकवर्तिका .. 107 ..
16.166.m: There should be cakes filled with ghee and accompanied by abundant milk; / such cakes are to be made; the second is the aśokavartikā.

16.166.s:
tṛtīyā pūpikā kāryā kharjureṇa samanvitāḥ ..
caturthaścaiva saṃyāvo guḍājyābhyāṃ samanvitaḥ .. .. 108 ..
16.166.d:
तृतीया पूपिका कार्या खर्जुरेण समन्विताः ..
चतुर्थश्चैव संयावो गुडाज्याभ्यां समन्वितः .. .. 108 ..
16.166.m: The third pastry should be made accompanied by dates; / and the fourth is the saṃyāva dish, prepared with molasses and ghee.

16.166.s:
āhlādakāriṇī puṃsāṃ strīṇāṃ cātīva vallabhā ..
dhanadhānyajanopetaṃ nārīnaraśatākulam ..
pūpakaistu kulaṃ tasyā jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. .. 109 ..
16.166.d:
आह्लादकारिणी पुंसां स्त्रीणां चातीव वल्लभा ..
धनधान्यजनोपेतं नारीनरशताकुलम् ..
पूपकैस्तु कुलं तस्या जायते नात्र संशयः .. .. 109 ..
16.166.m: It brings delight to men and is exceedingly dear to women. / Endowed with wealth, grain, and people, crowded with hundreds of women and men, / her family becomes such through cakes; there is no doubt about this.

16.166.s:
na jvaro na ca saṃtāpo duḥkhaṃ ca na viyogajam ..
aśokavartidānena kulānāmekaviṃśatiḥ .. 7.1.166.110 ..
16.166.d:
न ज्वरो न च संतापो दुःखं च न वियोगजम् ..
अशोकवर्तिदानेन कुलानामेकविंशतिः .. 7.1.166.110 ..
16.166.m: There is no fever, no burning torment, and no grief born of separation / for twenty-one generations through the gift of the aśokavarti.

16.166.s:
vadhūbhiśca sutaiścaiva dāsīdāsairanantakaiḥ ..
pūritaṃ ca kulaṃ tasyāḥ pūrikā yā prayacchati .. 111 ..
16.166.d:
वधूभिश्च सुतैश्चैव दासीदासैरनन्तकैः ..
पूरितं च कुलं तस्याः पूरिका या प्रयच्छति .. 111 ..
16.166.m: Filled with daughters-in-law, sons, and countless female and male servants / is the family of her who gives pūrikā cakes.

16.166.s:
putriṇyo vai duhitaro vadhūbhiḥ sahitāḥ kule ..
śikhariṇīpradātrīṇāṃ yuvatīnāṃ na saṃśayaḥ .. 112 ..
16.166.d:
पुत्रिण्यो वै दुहितरो वधूभिः सहिताः कुले ..
शिखरिणीप्रदात्रीणां युवतीनां न संशयः .. 112 ..
16.166.m: Daughters having sons along with daughters-in-law [abound] in the family / of young women who give śikhariṇī; of this there is no doubt.

16.166.s:
modate ca kulaṃ sarvaṃ sarvasiddhiprapūritam ..
modakānāṃ pradānena evamāha pitāmahaḥ .. 113 ..
16.166.d:
मोदते च कुलं सर्वं सर्वसिद्धिप्रपूरितम् ..
मोदकानां प्रदानेन एवमाह पितामहः .. 113 ..
16.166.m: And the whole family rejoices, filled with all accomplishments, / through the donation of modakas: so spoke the Grandfather.

16.166.s: etacca gauriṇīnāṃ tu bhojanaṃ hi viśiṣyate .. 114 ..
16.166.d: एतच्च गौरिणीनां तु भोजनं हि विशिष्यते .. 114 ..
16.166.m: And this meal is praised particularly for married women.

16.166.s:
subhagā putriṇī sādhvī dhanaṛddhisamanvitā ..
sahasrabhojinī devi bhavejjanmanijanmani .. 115 ..
16.166.d:
सुभगा पुत्रिणी साध्वी धनऋद्धिसमन्विता ..
सहस्रभोजिनी देवि भवेज्जन्मनिजन्मनि .. 115 ..
16.166.m: She becomes fortunate, blessed with sons, chaste, endowed with wealth and prosperity, / and feeds thousands, O goddess, in birth after birth. // 115

16.166.s:
pānāni caiva mukhyāni hṛdyāni madhurāṇi ca ..
drākṣāpānaṃ tu ciṃcāyāḥ pānaṃ guḍasamanvitam .. 116 ..
16.166.d:
पानानि चैव मुख्यानि हृद्यानि मधुराणि च ..
द्राक्षापानं तु चिंचायाः पानं गुडसमन्वितम् .. 116 ..
16.166.m: And chief drinks, delightful and sweet: / grape juice, and tamarind drink mixed with jaggery, // 116

16.166.s:
sarasena tu toyena kṛtakhaṇḍena vai śubham ..
suvāsinīnāṃ peyaṃ vai dātavyaṃ ca dvijanmanām .. 117 ..
16.166.d:
सरसेन तु तोयेन कृतखण्डेन वै शुभम् ..
सुवासिनीनां पेयं वै दातव्यं च द्विजन्मनाम् .. 117 ..
16.166.m: and delicious sugar beverage prepared with fragrant water / should certainly be offered as a drink to married women and to twice-born men. // 117

16.166.s:
itarairitarāṇyeva varṇayogyāni yāni ca ..
surabhīṇi ca pānāni tāsu yogyāni dāpayet .. 118 ..
16.166.d:
इतरैरितराण्येव वर्णयोग्यानि यानि च ..
सुरभीणि च पानानि तासु योग्यानि दापयेत् .. 118 ..
16.166.m: By other [castes] should be offered other fragrant drinks / suitable for [their] caste, whatever is appropriate for them. // 118

16.166.s:
pratipūjya vidhānena vastradānaiḥ sakaṃcukaiḥ ..
kuṅkumenānuliptāṃgāḥ sragdāmabhiralaṃkṛtāḥ ..
gaṃdhairdhūpaiśca saṃpūjya nālikerānpradāpayet .. 119 ..
16.166.d:
प्रतिपूज्य विधानेन वस्त्रदानैः सकंचुकैः ..
कुङ्कुमेनानुलिप्तांगाः स्रग्दामभिरलंकृताः ..
गंधैर्धूपैश्च संपूज्य नालिकेरान्प्रदापयेत् .. 119 ..
16.166.m: Having honoured them according to the rule with gifts of clothes including bodices, / their limbs anointed with saffron, adorned with garlands of flowers, / and having worshiped them with scents and incenses, one should offer coconuts. // 119

16.166.s:
netrāṇāṃ cāñjanaṃ kṛtvā sindūraṃ caiva mastake ..
pūgīphalāni hṛdyāni vāsitāni mṛdūni ca ..
haste dattvā sapātrāṇi praṇipatya visarjayet .. 7.1.166.120 ..
16.166.d:
नेत्राणां चाञ्जनं कृत्वा सिन्दूरं चैव मस्तके ..
पूगीफलानि हृद्यानि वासितानि मृदूनि च ..
हस्ते दत्त्वा सपात्राणि प्रणिपत्य विसर्जयेत् .. 7.1.166.120 ..
16.166.m: Having applied collyrium to their eyes and vermilion on their forehead, / placing delightful, scented, and soft betel nuts / in their hands along with vessels, one should bow down and bid them farewell. // 120

16.166.s:
svayaṃ ca bhojayetpaścādbaṃdhubhirbālakaiḥ saha .. 121 ..
athavā naiva saṃpadyettīrthe caiva tu bhojanam ..
gṛhe gatvā prabhoktavyaṃ tuṣṭā devī yathā bhavet .. 112 ..
16.166.d:
स्वयं च भोजयेत्पश्चाद्बंधुभिर्बालकैः सह .. 121 ..
अथवा नैव संपद्येत्तीर्थे चैव तु भोजनम् ..
गृहे गत्वा प्रभोक्तव्यं तुष्टा देवी यथा भवेत् .. 112 ..
16.166.m:
Afterward, one should eat oneself along with relatives and children. // 121
Or, if the meal cannot be arranged at the sacred ford, / one should go home and eat, so that the goddess may be pleased. // 122

16.166.s:
evameva pitṝṇāṃ ca āgamya sve ca mandire ..
piṇḍapradānapūrvaṃ tu śrāddhaṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ ..
pitarastasya tuṣṭā vai bhavanti brahmaṇo dinam ..123..
16.166.d:
एवमेव पितॄणां च आगम्य स्वे च मन्दिरे ..
पिण्डप्रदानपूर्वं तु श्राद्धं कृत्वा विधानतः ..
पितरस्तस्य तुष्टा वै भवन्ति ब्रह्मणो दिनम् ..123..
16.166.m: In this very manner, having returned to one's own house, / and having performed the śrāddha for the ancestors preceded by the offering of piṇḍas according to the rule, / his ancestors indeed remain satisfied for a day of Brahmā. // 123

16.166.s:
tīrthādaṣṭaguṇaṃ puṇyaṃ svagṛhe dadataḥ śubhe ..
na ca paśyanti vai nīcāḥ śrāddhaṃ dattaṃ dvijātibhiḥ .. 124 ..
16.166.d:
तीर्थादष्टगुणं पुण्यं स्वगृहे ददतः शुभे ..
न च पश्यन्ति वै नीचाः श्राद्धं दत्तं द्विजातिभिः .. 124 ..
16.166.m: The merit of giving in one's own auspicious home is eight times greater than at a sacred ford, / and vile persons do not look upon the śrāddha offered by the twice-born. // 124

16.166.s:
ekānte tu gṛhe gupte pitṝṇāṃ śrāddhamiṣyate ..
nīcaṃ dṛṣṭvā hataṃ tattu pitṝṇāṃ nopatiṣṭhati .. 125 ..
16.166.d:
एकान्ते तु गृहे गुप्ते पितॄणां श्राद्धमिष्यते ..
नीचं दृष्ट्वा हतं तत्तु पितॄणां नोपतिष्ठति .. 125 ..
16.166.m: The śrāddha for the ancestors is desired [to be performed] in a secluded, secret house; / destroyed when seen by a base person, it does not reach the ancestors. // 125

16.166.s:
tasmātsarvaprayatnena śrāddhaṃ guptaṃ ca kārayet ..
pitṝṇāṃ tṛptidaṃ proktaṃ svayameva svayaṃbhuvā ..126..
16.166.d:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन श्राद्धं गुप्तं च कारयेत् ..
पितॄणां तृप्तिदं प्रोक्तं स्वयमेव स्वयंभुवा ..126..
16.166.m: Therefore, with every effort, one should perform the śrāddha secretly; / it is declared by the Self-manifest [Brahmā] himself to bring satisfaction to the ancestors. // 126

16.166.s:
gaurībhojyādikā yā tu utsargātkriyate kriyā ..
rājasī sā samākhyātā janānāṃ kīrtidāyinī .. 127 ..
16.166.d:
गौरीभोज्यादिका या तु उत्सर्गात्क्रियते क्रिया ..
राजसी सा समाख्याता जनानां कीर्तिदायिनी .. 127 ..
16.166.m: The ritual such as feeding [girls representing] Gaurī, which is performed publicly, / is declared to be rājasika, granting fame among people. // 127

16.166.s:
idaṃ dānaṃ sadā deyamātmano hita micchatā ..
śrāddhe caiva viśeṣeṇa yadīcchetsāttvikaṃ phalam .. 128 ..
16.166.d:
इदं दानं सदा देयमात्मनो हित मिच्छता ..
श्राद्धे चैव विशेषेण यदीच्छेत्सात्त्विकं फलम् .. 128 ..
16.166.m: This gift should always be given by one who desires his own welfare, / and especially in a śrāddha, if one desires a sāttvika fruit. // 128

16.166.s:
idamudyāpanaṃ devi sāvitryāstu vratasya ca ..
sarvapātakaśuddhyarthaṃ kāryaṃ devi naraiḥ sadā ..
akāmataḥ kāmato vā pāpaṃ naśyati tatkṣaṇāt .. 129 ..
16.166.d:
इदमुद्यापनं देवि सावित्र्यास्तु व्रतस्य च ..
सर्वपातकशुद्ध्यर्थं कार्यं देवि नरैः सदा ..
अकामतः कामतो वा पापं नश्यति तत्क्षणात् .. 129 ..
16.166.m: This concluding rite of the vow of Sāvitrī, O goddess, / should always be performed by men to purify all sins; / whether unintentionally or intentionally, sin is destroyed in that very moment. // 129

16.166.s:
iha loke tu saubhāgyaṃ dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ varāḥ striyaḥ ..
bhavaṃti vividhāsteṣāṃ yairyātrā tatra vai kṛtā .. 7.1.166.130 ..
16.166.d:
इह लोके तु सौभाग्यं धनं धान्यं वराः स्त्रियः ..
भवंति विविधास्तेषां यैर्यात्रा तत्र वै कृता .. 7.1.166.130 ..
16.166.m: In this world, good fortune, wealth, grain, and excellent wives / of various kinds belong to those by whom the pilgrimage was made there. // 130

16.166.s:
idaṃ yātrāvidhānaṃ tu bhaktyā yaḥ kurute naraḥ ..
śṛṇoti vā sa pāpaistu sarvaireva pramucyate .. 131 ..
16.166.d:
इदं यात्राविधानं तु भक्त्या यः कुरुते नरः ..
शृणोति वा स पापैस्तु सर्वैरेव प्रमुच्यते .. 131 ..
16.166.m: The man who performs this rite of pilgrimage with devotion / or hears it is freed from all sins. // 131

16.166.s:
jyeṣṭhasya pūrṇimāyāṃ tu sāvitrīsthalake śubhe ..
pradakṣiṇā yaḥ kurute phaladānairyathāvidhi .. 132 ..
16.166.d:
ज्येष्ठस्य पूर्णिमायां तु सावित्रीस्थलके शुभे ..
प्रदक्षिणा यः कुरुते फलदानैर्यथाविधि .. 132 ..
16.166.m: On the full moon of the month of Jyeṣṭha, at the auspicious place of Sāvitrī, / he who performs circumambulation according to the rule with offerings of fruits, // 132

16.166.s:
aṣṭottaraśataṃ vāpi tadardhārdhaṃ tadardhakam ..
yaḥ karoti naro devi sṛṣṭvā tatra pradakṣiṇām .. 133 ..
16.166.d:
अष्टोत्तरशतं वापि तदर्धार्धं तदर्धकम् ..
यः करोति नरो देवि सृष्ट्वा तत्र प्रदक्षिणाम् .. 133 ..
16.166.m: either one hundred and eight times, or half of that, or half of that, / whichever man performs circumambulations there, O goddess, // 133

16.166.s:
agamyāgamanaṃ yaiśca kṛtaṃ jñānācca mānavaiḥ ..
anyāni pātakānyevaṃ naśyaṃte nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 134 ..
16.166.d:
अगम्यागमनं यैश्च कृतं ज्ञानाच्च मानवैः ..
अन्यानि पातकान्येवं नश्यंते नात्र संशयः .. 134 ..
16.166.m: if men have committed intercourse with forbidden women knowingly, / such and other sins are destroyed; of this there is no doubt. // 134

16.166.s:
yairgatvā sthalake saṃdhyā sāvitryāḥ samupāsitā ..
svapatnyāścaiva hastena pāṃḍukūpajalena ca .. 135 ..
16.166.d:
यैर्गत्वा स्थलके संध्या सावित्र्याः समुपासिता ..
स्वपत्न्याश्चैव हस्तेन पांडुकूपजलेन च .. 135 ..
16.166.m: By those who, having gone to the sacred place of Sāvitrī, have performed the twilight worship / using water from the Pāṇḍukūpa well by the hand of their own wife, // 135

16.166.s:
bhṛṃgārakanakenaiva mṛnmayenātha bhāmini ..
ānīya tu jalaṃ puṇyaṃ saṃdhyopāstiṃ karoti yaḥ ..
tena dvādaśavarṣāṇi bhavetsaṃdhyā hyupāsitā .. 136 ..
16.166.d:
भृंगारकनकेनैव मृन्मयेनाथ भामिनि ..
आनीय तु जलं पुण्यं संध्योपास्तिं करोति यः ..
तेन द्वादशवर्षाणि भवेत्संध्या ह्युपासिता .. 136 ..
16.166.m: bringing the sacred water in a golden pitcher or an earthen one, O passionate woman, / whoever performs the twilight worship, / by him the twilight worship has indeed been performed for twelve years. // 136

16.166.s:
aśvamedhaphalaṃ snāne dāne daśaguṇaṃ tathā ..
upavāse tvanaṃtaṃ ca kathāyāḥ śravaṇe tathā .. 137 ..
16.166.d:
अश्वमेधफलं स्नाने दाने दशगुणं तथा ..
उपवासे त्वनंतं च कथायाः श्रवणे तथा .. 137 ..
16.166.m: The fruit of a horse-sacrifice is obtained by ablution, ten times that by donation, / infinite by fasting, and likewise by hearing the sacred story. // 137

16.166.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsa khaṇḍe prathame prabhāsakṣetramāhātmye sāvitrīvratavidhipūjanaprakārodyāpanādikathanaṃnāma ṣaṭṣaṣṭyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 166 ..
16.166.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभास खण्डे प्रथमे प्रभासक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये सावित्रीव्रतविधिपूजनप्रकारोद्यापनादिकथनंनाम षट्षष्ट्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः .. 166 ..
16.166.m: Thus ends the one hundred and sixty-sixth chapter, named 'The Account of the Rules, Method of Worship, and Concluding Rite of the Vow of Sāvitrī', in the first [sub-section], the Prabhāsakṣetramāhātmya, of the seventh section, the Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. // 166

16.167.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
tato gacchenmahādevi tatrasthāṃ bhūtamātṛkām ..
sāvitryā vārūṇe bhāge śatadhanvaṃtare sthitām ..
navakoṭi gaṇairyuktāṃ pretabhūtasamākulām ..
pūjitāṃ siddhagaṃdharvairdevādibhiranekaśaḥ .. 2 ..
16.167.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
ततो गच्छेन्महादेवि तत्रस्थां भूतमातृकाम् ..
सावित्र्या वारूणे भागे शतधन्वंतरे स्थिताम् ..
नवकोटि गणैर्युक्तां प्रेतभूतसमाकुलाम् ..
पूजितां सिद्धगंधर्वैर्देवादिभिरनेकशः .. 2 ..
16.167.m: Īśvara said: / Then one should go, O great goddess, to Bhūtamātṛkā situated there, / standing a hundred dhanus to the west of Sāvitrī, / accompanied by ninety million gaṇas, crowded with spirits and ghosts, / worshiped manifoldly by siddhas, gandharvas, gods, and others. // 2

16.167.s:
.. devyuvāca .. ..
bhūtamāteti saṃhṛṣṭā grāmegrāme purepure ..
gāyannṛtyanhasam̐llokaḥ sarvataḥ paridhāvati .. 3 ..
16.167.d:
.. देव्युवाच .. ..
भूतमातेति संहृष्टा ग्रामेग्रामे पुरेपुरे ..
गायन्नृत्यन्हसम्̐ल्लोकः सर्वतः परिधावति .. 3 ..
16.167.m: The goddess said: / Shouting 'Mother of Spirits!', people rejoice in every village and town; / singing, dancing, and laughing, they run about in all directions. // 3

16.167.s:
unmattavatpralapate kṣitau patati mattavat ..
kruddhavaddhāvati parānmṛtavatkṛṣyate hi saḥ .. 4 ..
16.167.d:
उन्मत्तवत्प्रलपते क्षितौ पतति मत्तवत् ..
क्रुद्धवद्धावति परान्मृतवत्कृष्यते हि सः .. 4 ..
16.167.m: A person babbles like a madman, falls on the earth like a drunkard, / runs at others like one enraged, and is dragged like a corpse. // 4

16.167.s:
sukhabhaṃgāṃśca kurute loko vātagṛhītavat ..
bhūtavadbhasmamūtrāṃbukardamānavagāhate .. 5 ..
16.167.d:
सुखभंगांश्च कुरुते लोको वातगृहीतवत् ..
भूतवद्भस्ममूत्रांबुकर्दमानवगाहते .. 5 ..
16.167.m: Like one possessed by wind, people convulse with spasms, / and like spirits they plunge into ash, urine, water, and mud. // 5

16.167.s:
kimeṣa śāstranirdiṣṭo mārgaḥ kimuta laukikaḥ ..
muhyate me mano deva tena tvaṃ vaktumarhasi .. 6 ..
16.167.d:
किमेष शास्त्रनिर्दिष्टो मार्गः किमुत लौकिकः ..
मुह्यते मे मनो देव तेन त्वं वक्तुमर्हसि .. 6 ..
16.167.m: Is this a path prescribed by the scriptures, or is it merely worldly? / My mind is bewildered, O Lord; therefore, you ought to speak. // 6

16.167.s:
kathaṃ sā puruṣaiḥ pūjyā prabhāsakṣetravāsibhiḥ ..
kasmāttatra gatā devī kasminkāle samāgatā ..
kasmindine tu māse tu tasyāḥ kāryo mahotsavaḥ .. 7 ..
16.167.d:
कथं सा पुरुषैः पूज्या प्रभासक्षेत्रवासिभिः ..
कस्मात्तत्र गता देवी कस्मिन्काले समागता ..
कस्मिन्दिने तु मासे तु तस्याः कार्यो महोत्सवः .. 7 ..
16.167.m: How should she be worshiped by men dwelling in Prabhāsa sacred field? / Why did that goddess go there? At what time did she arrive? / On what day and in which month should her great festival be celebrated? // 7

16.167.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi yatte kiṃcinmanogatam ..
āstikāḥ śraddadhānāśca bhavantīti matirmama .. 8 ..
16.167.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
शृणु देवि प्रवक्ष्यामि यत्ते किंचिन्मनोगतम् ..
आस्तिकाः श्रद्दधानाश्च भवन्तीति मतिर्मम .. 8 ..
16.167.m: Īśvara said: / Listen, O goddess, I shall explain whatever is in your mind; / my conviction is that [such people] are faithful and endowed with belief. // 8

16.167.s:
cākṣuṣasyāntare'tīte prāpte vaivasvate'ntare ..
dakṣāpamānātsaṃjātā tadā parvataputrikā .. 9 ..
16.167.d:
चाक्षुषस्यान्तरेऽतीते प्राप्ते वैवस्वतेऽन्तरे ..
दक्षापमानात्संजाता तदा पर्वतपुत्रिका .. 9 ..
16.167.m: When the interval of Cākṣuṣa had passed and the interval of Vaivasvata had arrived, / then, because of the insult by Dakṣa, the Daughter of the Mountain was born. // 9

16.167.s:
dvāpare tu dvitīye vai dattā tvaṃ parvatena me ..
vivāhe caiva saṃjāte sarvadevamanorame .. 7.1.167.10 ..
16.167.d:
द्वापरे तु द्वितीये वै दत्ता त्वं पर्वतेन मे ..
विवाहे चैव संजाते सर्वदेवमनोरमे .. 7.1.167.10 ..
16.167.m: In the second Dvāpara age, you were indeed given to me by the Mountain, / and a marriage delightful to all the gods took place. // 10

16.167.s:
tvayā ca sahitaḥ pūrvaṃ mandare cārukaṃdare ..
akrīḍaṃ ca mudā yukto divyakrīḍanakaiḥ priye ..
pīnonnatanitaṃbena bhrājamānā kuconnatām .. 11 ..
16.167.d:
त्वया च सहितः पूर्वं मन्दरे चारुकंदरे ..
अक्रीडं च मुदा युक्तो दिव्यक्रीडनकैः प्रिये ..
पीनोन्नतनितंबेन भ्राजमाना कुचोन्नताम् .. 11 ..
16.167.m: Formerly, together with you in the beautiful caves of Mount Mandara, / I sported with delight using celestial playthings, O beloved, / you who were shining with large, raised hips and prominent breasts. // 11

16.167.s:
sitābjavadanāṃ hṛṣṭāṃ dṛṣṭvā'haṃ tvāṃ mahāprabhām ..
dagdhakāmataroḥ kandakaṃdalīmiva niḥsṛtām ..
mahārhaśayanasthāṃ tvāṃ tadā kāmitavānaham .. 12 ..
16.167.d:
सिताब्जवदनां हृष्टां दृष्ट्वाऽहं त्वां महाप्रभाम् ..
दग्धकामतरोः कन्दकंदलीमिव निःसृताम् ..
महार्हशयनस्थां त्वां तदा कामितवानहम् .. 12 ..
16.167.m: Seeing you joyous, with a face like a white lotus and radiant with great splendour, / like a shoot emerging from the bulb of the burnt tree of Desire, / resting upon a precious bed, I then made love to you. // 12

16.167.s:
surate tava saṃjātaṃ divyaṃ varṣaśataṃ yadā ..
tadā devi samutthāya nirodhānnirgatā bahiḥ .. .. 13 ..
16.167.d:
सुरते तव संजातं दिव्यं वर्षशतं यदा ..
तदा देवि समुत्थाय निरोधान्निर्गता बहिः .. .. 13 ..
16.167.m: When a hundred celestial years had elapsed in your sexual embrace, / then, O goddess, rising up from the embrace, you went outside. // 13

16.167.s:
tavodakātsamuttasthau nāryekā gahvarodarā ..
kṛṣṇā karālavadanā piṃgākṣī muktamūrdhajā .. 14 ..
16.167.d:
तवोदकात्समुत्तस्थौ नार्येका गह्वरोदरा ..
कृष्णा करालवदना पिंगाक्षी मुक्तमूर्धजा .. 14 ..
16.167.m: From your water there arose a woman with a hollow belly, / black, with a terrifying face, reddish-brown eyes, and disheveled hair, // 14

16.167.s:
kapālamālābharaṇā baddhamuṇḍārdhapiṃḍakā ..
khaṭvāṃgakaṃkāladharā ruṇḍamuṃḍakarā śivā .. 15 ..
16.167.d:
कपालमालाभरणा बद्धमुण्डार्धपिंडका ..
खट्वांगकंकालधरा रुण्डमुंडकरा शिवा .. 15 ..
16.167.m: adorned with a garland of skulls, with half-lumps of severed heads tied [to her], / holding a skull-topped staff and a skeleton, carrying headless trunks and severed heads in her hands, auspicious. // 15

16.167.s:
dvīpicarmāmbaradharā raṇatkiṃkiṇimekhalā ..
ḍamaḍḍamarukārā ca phetkārapūritāmbarā .. 16 ..
16.167.d:
द्वीपिचर्माम्बरधरा रणत्किंकिणिमेखला ..
डमड्डमरुकारा च फेत्कारपूरिताम्बरा .. 16 ..
16.167.m: wearing a leopard-skin garment, with a girdle of ringing bells, / making the sound of a *ḍamaru* drum, and filling the sky with howling shrieks. // 16

16.167.s:
tasyāśca pārśvagā anyāstāsāṃ nāmāni me śṛṇu ..
sakhyo brāhmaṇarākṣasyastāsāṃ caiva sudarśanāḥ .. 17 ..
16.167.d:
तस्याश्च पार्श्वगा अन्यास्तासां नामानि मे शृणु ..
सख्यो ब्राह्मणराक्षस्यस्तासां चैव सुदर्शनाः .. 17 ..
16.167.m: And there were others standing at her side—hear their names from me: / female companions, Brahmin-rākṣasīs, fair to look upon. // 17

16.167.s:
daśakoṭiprabhedena dharāṃ vyāpya susaṃsthitāḥ ..
mukhyāstatra catasro vai mahābalaparākramāḥ .. 18 ..
16.167.d:
दशकोटिप्रभेदेन धरां व्याप्य सुसंस्थिताः ..
मुख्यास्तत्र चतस्रो वै महाबलपराक्रमाः .. 18 ..
16.167.m: Divided into a hundred million varieties, they stood pervading the earth; / four among them were foremost, possessed of great strength and valor: // 18

16.167.s:
raktavarṇā mahājihvā'kṣayā vai pāpakāriṇī ..
etāsāmanvaye jātāḥ pṛthivyāṃ brahmarākṣasāḥ .. 19 ..
16.167.d:
रक्तवर्णा महाजिह्वाऽक्षया वै पापकारिणी ..
एतासामन्वये जाताः पृथिव्यां ब्रह्मराक्षसाः .. 19 ..
16.167.m: Raktavarṇā, Mahājihvā, Akṣayā, and Pāpakāriṇī. / From their lineage were born the brahmarākṣasas upon earth. // 19

16.167.s:
śleṣmātakatarau hyete prāyaśaḥ sukṛtālayāḥ ..
uttālatālacapalā nṛtyaṃti ca hasaṃti ca .. 7.1.167.20 ..
16.167.d:
श्लेष्मातकतरौ ह्येते प्रायशः सुकृतालयाः ..
उत्तालतालचपला नृत्यंति च हसंति च .. 7.1.167.20 ..
16.167.m: They usually make their dwelling in the *śleṣmātaka* tree; / agitated like lofty palm trees, they dance and laugh. // 20

16.167.s:
vijñeyā iha loke'sminbhūtānāṃ mūlanāyakāḥ ..
atikṛṣṇā bhavantyete vyaṃtarāntaracāriṇaḥ .. 21 ..
16.167.d:
विज्ञेया इह लोकेऽस्मिन्भूतानां मूलनायकाः ..
अतिकृष्णा भवन्त्येते व्यंतरान्तरचारिणः .. 21 ..
16.167.m: They are to be known as the chief leaders of spirits in this world; / extremely dark, they wander among intermediary realms. // 21

16.167.s: vṛkṣāgramātramākāśaṃ te caraṃti na saṃśayaḥ .. .. 22 ..
16.167.d: वृक्षाग्रमात्रमाकाशं ते चरंति न संशयः .. .. 22 ..
16.167.m: They roam the space of the sky just to the height of treetops, without a doubt. // 22

16.167.s:
tathaiva mama vīryāttu madrūpābharaṇaḥ pumān ..
kapālakhaṭvāṃgadharo jātaścarmaviguṇṭhitaḥ .. 23 ..
16.167.d:
तथैव मम वीर्यात्तु मद्रूपाभरणः पुमान् ..
कपालखट्वांगधरो जातश्चर्मविगुण्ठितः .. 23 ..
16.167.m: Likewise, indeed from my seed, a male was born bearing my form and ornaments, / holding a skull-bowl and a skull-staff, and wrapped in an animal skin. // 23

16.167.s:
anugamyamāno bahubhirbhūtairapi bhayaṃkaraḥ ..
siṃhaśārdūlavadanairvadanollikhitāṃbaraiḥ .. 24 ..
16.167.d:
अनुगम्यमानो बहुभिर्भूतैरपि भयंकरः ..
सिंहशार्दूलवदनैर्वदनोल्लिखितांबरैः .. 24 ..
16.167.m: He was followed by many fearsome spirits / with the faces of lions and tigers, scratching the sky with their faces. // 24

16.167.s:
evaṃ devi tadā jātaḥ kṣudhākrānto babhāṣa mām ..
ato'haṃ kṣudhitaṃ dṛṣṭvā varaṃ hīmaṃ ca dattavān .. 25 ..
16.167.d:
एवं देवि तदा जातः क्षुधाक्रान्तो बभाष माम् ..
अतोऽहं क्षुधितं दृष्ट्वा वरं हीमं च दत्तवान् .. 25 ..
16.167.m: Thus born then, O goddess, overcome by hunger, he spoke to me. / Therefore, seeing him hungry, I granted him this boon: // 25

16.167.s:
yuvayorhastasaṃsparśānnaktamevāstu sarvaśaḥ ..
naktaṃ caiva balīyāṃsau divā nātibalāvubhau ..
putravadrakṣataṃ lokāndharmaścaivānupālyatām .. .. 26 ..
16.167.d:
युवयोर्हस्तसंस्पर्शान्नक्तमेवास्तु सर्वशः ..
नक्तं चैव बलीयांसौ दिवा नातिबलावुभौ ..
पुत्रवद्रक्षतं लोकान्धर्मश्चैवानुपाल्यताम् .. .. 26 ..
16.167.m: ‘Let everything take place for both of you entirely at night through the touch of your hands; / and at night you two shall be mighty, but by day not very strong. / Protect the worlds like sons, and let dharma be preserved.’ // 26

16.167.s:
ityuktau tau mayā tatra bhūtamātṛgaṇau priye ..
ekībhūtau kṣaṇenaiva tau bhavānībhavodbhavau .. 27 ..
16.167.d:
इत्युक्तौ तौ मया तत्र भूतमातृगणौ प्रिये ..
एकीभूतौ क्षणेनैव तौ भवानीभवोद्भवौ .. 27 ..
16.167.m: When those two—the host of spirits and mothers—had thus been addressed by me there, my dear, / born from Bhavānī and Bhava, they became united in a single moment. // 27

16.167.s: dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭamanāścāhamavocaṃ tvāṃ śucismite .. 28 ..
16.167.d: दृष्ट्वा हृष्टमनाश्चाहमवोचं त्वां शुचिस्मिते .. 28 ..
16.167.m: Seeing them, I was delighted in mind and said to you, O lady of pure smiles: // 28

16.167.s:
kalyāṇi paśyapaśyaitau mamāṃśācca samudbhavau ..
bībhatsādbhutaśṛṃgāradhāriṇau hāsyakāriṇau ..29..
16.167.d:
कल्याणि पश्यपश्यैतौ ममांशाच्च समुद्भवौ ..
बीभत्साद्भुतशृंगारधारिणौ हास्यकारिणौ ..29..
16.167.m: ‘O auspicious one, see, see these two born from my portion, / bearing the repulsive, the marvelous, and the erotic, provoking laughter! // 29

16.167.s:
bhrātṛbhāṃḍā bhūtamātā tathaivodakasevitā ..
saṃjñātrayaṃ smṛtaṃ devi loke vikhyātapauruṣam ..7.1.167.30..
16.167.d:
भ्रातृभांडा भूतमाता तथैवोदकसेविता ..
संज्ञात्रयं स्मृतं देवि लोके विख्यातपौरुषम् ..7.1.167.30..
16.167.m: “Bhrātṛbhāṇḍā”, “Mother of Spirits”, and likewise “Attendant of the Waters”— / three names are remembered, O goddess, renowned in the world for their power.’ // 30

16.167.s:
punaḥ kṛtāṃjalipuṭau dṛṣṭvā māmūcatustadā ..
āvayorbhagavankutra sthāne vāso bhaviṣyati ..31..
16.167.d:
पुनः कृतांजलिपुटौ दृष्ट्वा मामूचतुस्तदा ..
आवयोर्भगवन्कुत्र स्थाने वासो भविष्यति ..31..
16.167.m: Having folded their hands in reverence again upon seeing me, they then spoke: / ‘O Lord, in which place will our dwelling be?’ // 31

16.167.s:
ityuktavantau tau tatra vareṇa cchanditau mayā ..
asti saurāṣṭraviṣaye bhārate kṣetramuttamam ..32..
16.167.d:
इत्युक्तवन्तौ तौ तत्र वरेण च्छन्दितौ मया ..
अस्ति सौराष्ट्रविषये भारते क्षेत्रमुत्तमम् ..32..
16.167.m: When they had spoken thus, they were indulged there by me with a boon: / ‘There is in the region of Saurāṣṭra, in Bhārata, an excellent sacred field, // 32

16.167.s:
prabhāseti samākhyātaṃ tatra kṣemaṃ mama priyam ..
kūrmasya nairṛte bhāge sthitaṃ vai dakṣiṇe pare..33..
16.167.d:
प्रभासेति समाख्यातं तत्र क्षेमं मम प्रियम् ..
कूर्मस्य नैरृते भागे स्थितं वै दक्षिणे परे..33..
16.167.m: renowned as Prabhāsa; there is peace, dear to me. / It is situated in the southwest portion of the Tortoise, in the far south, // 33

16.167.s:
svātī viśākhā maitraṃ ca yatra ṛkṣatrayaṃ smṛtam..
tasminsthāne sadā stheyaṃ yāvanmanvantarāvadhi..34..
16.167.d:
स्वाती विशाखा मैत्रं च यत्र ऋक्षत्रयं स्मृतम्..
तस्मिन्स्थाने सदा स्थेयं यावन्मन्वन्तरावधि..34..
16.167.m: where the triad of asterisms is remembered as Svātī, Viśākhā, and Maitra. / In that place you must always reside until the end of the manvantara. // 34

16.167.s: anyadā jīvikaṃ vacmi tava bhūtapriye sadā .. 35 ..
16.167.d: अन्यदा जीविकं वच्मि तव भूतप्रिये सदा .. 35 ..
16.167.m: At other times, O lover of spirits, I declare your constant livelihood: // 35

16.167.s:
yatra kaṇṭakino vṛkṣā yatra niṣpāvavallarī ..
bhāryā punarbhūrvalmīkastāste vasatayaściram .. 36 ..
16.167.d:
यत्र कण्टकिनो वृक्षा यत्र निष्पाववल्लरी ..
भार्या पुनर्भूर्वल्मीकस्तास्ते वसतयश्चिरम् .. 36 ..
16.167.m: Where there are thorny trees, where there is a creeping flat-bean vine, / a remarried wife, and an ant-hill—those are your long-lasting dwellings. // 36

16.167.s:
yasmingṛhe narāḥ pañca strītrayaṃ tāvatīśca gāḥ ..
andhakāreṃdhanāgniśca tadgṛhe vasatistava .. 37 ..
16.167.d:
यस्मिन्गृहे नराः पञ्च स्त्रीत्रयं तावतीश्च गाः ..
अन्धकारेंधनाग्निश्च तद्गृहे वसतिस्तव .. 37 ..
16.167.m: In a house where there are five men, three women, and as many cows, / and a fire of wet fuel in darkness—in that house is your dwelling. // 37

16.167.s:
bhūtaiḥ pretaiḥ piśācaiśca yatsthānaṃ samadhiṣṭhitam ..
ekāvi cāṣṭabāleyaṃ trigavaṃ pañcamāhiṣam ..
ṣaḍaśvaṃ saptamātaṃgaṃ tadgṛhe vasatistava .. 38 ..
16.167.d:
भूतैः प्रेतैः पिशाचैश्च यत्स्थानं समधिष्ठितम् ..
एकावि चाष्टबालेयं त्रिगवं पञ्चमाहिषम् ..
षडश्वं सप्तमातंगं तद्गृहे वसतिस्तव .. 38 ..
16.167.m: A place inhabited by bhūtas, pretas, and piśācas, / [a house with] one sheep, eight donkeys, three cows, five buffaloes, / six horses, and seven elephants—in that house is your dwelling. // 38

16.167.s:
uddālakānnapiṭakaṃ tadvatsthālyādibhājanam ..
yatra tatraiva kṣiptaṃ ca tava tacca pratiśrayam .. 39 ..
16.167.d:
उद्दालकान्नपिटकं तद्वत्स्थाल्यादिभाजनम् ..
यत्र तत्रैव क्षिप्तं च तव तच्च प्रतिश्रयम् .. 39 ..
16.167.m: A basket of wild grain, likewise vessels such as cooking pots, / wherever thrown carelessly here and there—that is your shelter. // 39

16.167.s:
muśalolūkhale strīṇāmāsyā tadvaduduṃbare ..
bhāṣaṇaṃ kaṭukaṃ caiva tatra devi sthitistava .. 7.1.167.40 ..
16.167.d:
मुशलोलूखले स्त्रीणामास्या तद्वदुदुंबरे ..
भाषणं कटुकं चैव तत्र देवि स्थितिस्तव .. 7.1.167.40 ..
16.167.m: Where women sit on the pestle and mortar, and likewise on the threshold, / and where there is harsh speech—there, O goddess, is your abode. // 40

16.167.s:
khādyante yatra dhānyāni pakvāpakvāni veśmani ..
tadvacchākhāśca tatra tvaṃ bhūtaiḥ saha cariṣyasi .. 41 ..
16.167.d:
खाद्यन्ते यत्र धान्यानि पक्वापक्वानि वेश्मनि ..
तद्वच्छाखाश्च तत्र त्वं भूतैः सह चरिष्यसि .. 41 ..
16.167.m: In a house where grains, whether cooked or uncooked, are eaten, / and likewise their stalks—there you shall wander together with spirits. // 41

16.167.s:
sthālīpidhāne yatrāgniṃ dadate vikalā narāḥ ..
gṛhe tatra duriṣṭānāmaśeṣāṇāṃ samāśrayaḥ .. 42 ..
16.167.d:
स्थालीपिधाने यत्राग्निं ददते विकला नराः ..
गृहे तत्र दुरिष्टानामशेषाणां समाश्रयः .. 42 ..
16.167.m: Where agitated men place fire upon the lid of a cooking pot, / in that house is the refuge of all misfortune. // 42

16.167.s:
mānuṣyāsthi gṛhe yatra ahorātre vyavasthitam ..
tatrāyaṃ bhūtanivaho yatheṣṭaṃ vicariṣyati .. 43 ..
16.167.d:
मानुष्यास्थि गृहे यत्र अहोरात्रे व्यवस्थितम् ..
तत्रायं भूतनिवहो यथेष्टं विचरिष्यति .. 43 ..
16.167.m: In a house where a human bone remains day and night, / there this multitude of spirits shall wander at will. // 43

16.167.s:
sarvasmādadhikaṃ ye na pravadanti pinākinam ..
sādhāraṇaṃ vadaṃtyenaṃ tatra bhūtaiḥ samāviśa .. 44 ..
16.167.d:
सर्वस्मादधिकं ये न प्रवदन्ति पिनाकिनम् ..
साधारणं वदंत्येनं तत्र भूतैः समाविश .. 44 ..
16.167.m: Where people do not proclaim the Wielder of the Pināka Bow as superior to all, / but speak of him as ordinary—enter there together with the spirits! // 44

16.167.s:
kanyā ca yatra vai vallī rohīnāma jaṭī gṛhe ..
agastya pādapo vāpi baṃdhujīvo gṛheṣu vai .. 45 ..
16.167.d:
कन्या च यत्र वै वल्ली रोहीनाम जटी गृहे ..
अगस्त्य पादपो वापि बंधुजीवो गृहेषु वै .. 45 ..
16.167.m: In a house where there is the creeper called Kanyā, Rohī, or Jaṭī, / or an Agastya tree, or a Bandhujīva in their houses, // 45

16.167.s:
karavīro viśeṣeṇa naṃdyāvartastathaiva ca ..
mallikā vā gṛhe yeṣāṃ bhūtayogyaṃ gṛhaṃ hi tat .. 46 ..
16.167.d:
करवीरो विशेषेण नंद्यावर्तस्तथैव च ..
मल्लिका वा गृहे येषां भूतयोग्यं गृहं हि तत् .. 46 ..
16.167.m: especially the oleander, and likewise the Nandyāvarta, / or jasmine in their house—that house is indeed fit for spirits. // 46

16.167.s:
tālaṃ tamālaṃ bhallātaṃ tiṃtiṇīkhaṃḍameva vā ..
bakulaṃ kadalīkhaṃḍaṃ kadaṃbaḥ khadiro'pi vā ..47..
16.167.d:
तालं तमालं भल्लातं तिंतिणीखंडमेव वा ..
बकुलं कदलीखंडं कदंबः खदिरोऽपि वा ..47..
16.167.m: A palmyra, a tamāla, a bhallāta, or a grove of tamarind trees, / a bakula, a plantain grove, a kadamba, or even a khadira tree, // 47

16.167.s:
nyagrodho hi gṛhe yeṣāmaśvatthaṃ cūta eva vā ..
uduṃbaraśca panasaḥ sarvabhūta priyaṃ hi tat ..48..
16.167.d:
न्यग्रोधो हि गृहे येषामश्वत्थं चूत एव वा ..
उदुंबरश्च पनसः सर्वभूत प्रियं हि तत् ..48..
16.167.m: a banyan in the house of those who have it, or a sacred fig, or a mango, / a cluster fig, and a jackfruit—that is indeed dear to all spirits. // 48

16.167.s:
yatra kākagṛhaṃ vai syādārāme vā gṛhe'pi vā ..
bhikṣubiṃbaṃ ca vai yatra gṛhe dakṣiṇake tathā ..49..
16.167.d:
यत्र काकगृहं वै स्यादारामे वा गृहेऽपि वा ..
भिक्षुबिंबं च वै यत्र गृहे दक्षिणके तथा ..49..
16.167.m: Where there is a crow's nest, whether in a garden or in a house, / and where there is an image of an ascetic, likewise in the southern part of the house, // 49

16.167.s: biṃbamūrdhvaṃ ca yatrasthaṃ tatra bhūtaniveśanam ..7.1.167.50..
16.167.d: बिंबमूर्ध्वं च यत्रस्थं तत्र भूतनिवेशनम् ..7.1.167.50..
16.167.m: and where an image is set facing upward—there is the dwelling of spirits. // 50

16.167.s:
liṃgārcanaṃ na yatraiva yatra nāsti japādikam ..
yatra bhaktivihīnā vai bhūtānāṃ tāngṛhānvadet ..51..
16.167.d:
लिंगार्चनं न यत्रैव यत्र नास्ति जपादिकम् ..
यत्र भक्तिविहीना वै भूतानां तान्गृहान्वदेत् ..51..
16.167.m: Where there is no worship of the liṅga, where there is no recitation of mantras and the like, / where they are devoid of devotion—one should declare those to be houses of spirits. // 51

16.167.s:
malināsyāstu ye martyā malināṃbara dhāriṇaḥ ..
maladaṃtā gṛhasthā ye gṛhaṃ teṣāṃ samāviśa ..52..
16.167.d:
मलिनास्यास्तु ये मर्त्या मलिनांबर धारिणः ..
मलदंता गृहस्था ये गृहं तेषां समाविश ..52..
16.167.m: The mortals who have filthy faces, who wear dirty clothes, / the householders who have dirty teeth—enter their house! // 52

16.167.s:
agamyaniratā ye tu maithune vyabhicārataḥ ..
saṃdhyāyāṃ maithunaṃ yāṃti gṛhaṃ teṣāṃ samāviśa .. .. 53 ..
16.167.d:
अगम्यनिरता ये तु मैथुने व्यभिचारतः ..
संध्यायां मैथुनं यांति गृहं तेषां समाविश .. .. 53 ..
16.167.m: Those who indulge in forbidden intercourse through transgression, / and who engage in intercourse at twilight—enter their house! // 53

16.167.s:
bahunā kiṃ pralāpena nityakarmabahiṣkṛtāḥ ..
rudrabhaktivihīnā ye gṛhaṃ teṣāṃ samāviśa .. 54 ..
16.167.d:
बहुना किं प्रलापेन नित्यकर्मबहिष्कृताः ..
रुद्रभक्तिविहीना ये गृहं तेषां समाविश .. 54 ..
16.167.m: What need of much prattle? Those excluded from daily rites, / those devoid of devotion to Rudra—enter their house! // 54

16.167.s:
adattvā bhuṃjate yo'nnaṃ baṃdhubhyo'nnaṃ tathodakam ..
sapiṇḍānsodakāṃścaiva tatkālāttānnarānbhaja .. 55 ..
16.167.d:
अदत्त्वा भुंजते योऽन्नं बंधुभ्योऽन्नं तथोदकम् ..
सपिण्डान्सोदकांश्चैव तत्कालात्तान्नरान्भज .. 55 ..
16.167.m: He who eats food without giving food and water to his relatives, / to sapinda and sodaka kinsmen—seize those men immediately! // 55

16.167.s:
yatra bhāryā ca bhartā ca parasparavirodhinau ..
saha bhūtairgṛhaṃ tasya viśa tvaṃ bhayavarjjitā .. 56 ..
16.167.d:
यत्र भार्या च भर्ता च परस्परविरोधिनौ ..
सह भूतैर्गृहं तस्य विश त्वं भयवर्ज्जिता .. 56 ..
16.167.m: Where wife and husband are hostile to each other, / enter his house along with spirits, freed from fear. // 56

16.167.s:
vāsudeve ratirnāsti yatra nāsti sadā hariḥ ..
japahomādikaṃ nāsti bhasma nāsti gṛhe nṛṇām .. 57 ..
16.167.d:
वासुदेवे रतिर्नास्ति यत्र नास्ति सदा हरिः ..
जपहोमादिकं नास्ति भस्म नास्ति गृहे नृणाम् .. 57 ..
16.167.m: Where there is no delight in Vāsudeva, where Hari is never present, / where there is no recitation, oblation, and the like, and no sacred ash in the house of men, // 57

16.167.s: parvasvapyarcanaṃ nāsti caturdaśyāṃ viśeṣataḥ .. 58 ..
16.167.d: पर्वस्वप्यर्चनं नास्ति चतुर्दश्यां विशेषतः .. 58 ..
16.167.m: and where there is no worship even on festival days, especially on the fourteenth lunar day; // 58

16.167.s:
kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāṃ ca ye martyāḥ saṃdhyāyāṃ bhasmavarjitāḥ ..
paṃcadaśyāṃ mahādevaṃ na yajaṃti ca yatra vai ..59..
16.167.d:
कृष्णाष्टम्यां च ये मर्त्याः संध्यायां भस्मवर्जिताः ..
पंचदश्यां महादेवं न यजंति च यत्र वै ..59..
16.167.m: and the mortals who, on the dark eighth day, are devoid of sacred ash at twilight, / and where they do not worship Mahādeva on the fifteenth day; // 59

16.167.s:
paurajānapadairyatra prākprasiddhā mahotsavāḥ ..
kriyate pūrvavannaiva tadgṛhaṃ vasatistava .. 7.1.167.60 ..
16.167.d:
पौरजानपदैर्यत्र प्राक्प्रसिद्धा महोत्सवाः ..
क्रियते पूर्ववन्नैव तद्गृहं वसतिस्तव .. 7.1.167.60 ..
16.167.m: where the great festivals formerly celebrated by citizens and villagers / are no longer performed as before—that house is your dwelling.’ // 60

16.167.s:
vedaghoṣo na yatrāsti gurupūjādikaṃ na ca ..
pitṛkarmavihīnaṃ ca tadbhūtasya gṛhaṃ smṛtam ... .. 61 ..
16.167.d:
वेदघोषो न यत्रास्ति गुरुपूजादिकं न च ..
पितृकर्मविहीनं च तद्भूतस्य गृहं स्मृतम् ... .. 61 ..
16.167.m: Where there is no recitation of the Veda, and no worship of the guru and the like, / and where rites for the ancestors are neglected, that is regarded as a ghost's house. // 61

16.167.s:
rātraurātrau gṛhe yasminkalaho jāyate mithaḥ ..
bālānāṃ prekṣamāṇānāṃ yatra vṛddhaśca pūrvataḥ ..
bhakṣayettatra vai hṛṣṭā bhūtaiḥ saha samāviśa ..62..
16.167.d:
रात्रौरात्रौ गृहे यस्मिन्कलहो जायते मिथः ..
बालानां प्रेक्षमाणानां यत्र वृद्धश्च पूर्वतः ..
भक्षयेत्तत्र वै हृष्टा भूतैः सह समाविश ..62..
16.167.m: In whichever house quarrels arise between one another night after night, / while children watch, and where the elder eats beforehand— / enter there, joyful, together with the spirits! // 62

16.167.s:
kasminmāse dine cāpi bhavitrī lokapūjitā ..
ityukto'haṃ tayā devi tāmavocaṃ punaḥ priye ..63..
16.167.d:
कस्मिन्मासे दिने चापि भवित्री लोकपूजिता ..
इत्युक्तोऽहं तया देवि तामवोचं पुनः प्रिये ..63..
16.167.m: 'In which month and on which day will I be worshipped by the people?' / Thus addressed by her, O goddess, I spoke to her again, O beloved: // 63

16.167.s:
amā yā mādhave māsi tasminyā ca caturdaśī ..
tasyāṃ mahotsavastatra bhavitā te ciraṃtanaḥ..64..
16.167.d:
अमा या माधवे मासि तस्मिन्या च चतुर्दशी ..
तस्यां महोत्सवस्तत्र भविता ते चिरंतनः..64..
16.167.m: 'On the new moon day in the month of Mādhava, and on the fourteenth lunar day thereof, / on that [day] there will be your ancient grand festival. // 64

16.167.s:
yāḥ striyastāṃ ca yakṣyaṃti tasminkāle mahotsave..
balibhiḥ puṣpadhūpaiśca mā tāsāṃ tvaṃ gṛhe viśa..65..
16.167.d:
याः स्त्रियस्तां च यक्ष्यंति तस्मिन्काले महोत्सवे..
बलिभिः पुष्पधूपैश्च मा तासां त्वं गृहे विश..65..
16.167.m: Which women shall worship you at that time, during the grand festival, / with offerings, flowers, and incense—do not enter their house! // 65

16.167.s:
nārāyaṇa hṛṣīkeśa puṇḍarīkākṣa mādhava ..
acyutānaṃta goviṃda vāsudeva janārdana .. 66 ..
16.167.d:
नारायण हृषीकेश पुण्डरीकाक्ष माधव ..
अच्युतानंत गोविंद वासुदेव जनार्दन .. 66 ..
16.167.m: Those people who [call out]: 'O Nārāyaṇa, O Hṛṣīkeśa, O lotus-eyed one, O Mādhava! / O Acyuta, O Ananta, O Govinda, O Vāsudeva, O Janārdana! // 66

16.167.s:
nṛsiṃha vāmanāciṃtya keśaveti ca ye janāḥ ..
rudra rudreti rudreti śivāya ca namonamaḥ .. 67 ..
16.167.d:
नृसिंह वामनाचिंत्य केशवेति च ये जनाः ..
रुद्र रुद्रेति रुद्रेति शिवाय च नमोनमः .. 67 ..
16.167.m: O Nṛsiṃha, O Vāmana, O Inconceivable One, O Keśava!' / and: 'O Rudra, Rudra, Rudra! Reverence, reverence to Śiva!'— // 67

16.167.s:
vakṣyaṃti satataṃ hṛṣṭāsteṣāṃ dhanagṛhādiṣu ..
ārāme caiva goṣṭhe ca mā viśethāḥ kathaṃcana .. 68 ..
16.167.d:
वक्ष्यंति सततं हृष्टास्तेषां धनगृहादिषु ..
आरामे चैव गोष्ठे च मा विशेथाः कथंचन .. 68 ..
16.167.m: who constantly speak [these names] rejoicing—into their storehouses of wealth and the like, / into their garden, and into their cow-pen, by no means enter! // 68

16.167.s:
deśācārāñjñā tidharmāñjapaṃ homaṃ ca maṃgalam ..
daivatejyāṃ vidhānena śaucaṃ kurvaṃti ye janāḥ ..
lokāpavādabhītā ye pumāṃsasteṣu mā viśa ..69..
16.167.d:
देशाचाराञ्ज्ञा तिधर्माञ्जपं होमं च मंगलम् ..
दैवतेज्यां विधानेन शौचं कुर्वंति ये जनाः ..
लोकापवादभीता ये पुमांसस्तेषु मा विश ..69..
16.167.m: Those men who observe regional customs, caste duties, recitation, fire oblations, auspicious rites, / worship of the deities according to the rules, and bodily purity, / and those who are fearful of public disgrace—do not enter among them!' // 69

16.167.s:
.. devyuvāca ..
kadā pūjā prakartavyā bhūtamātuḥ sukhārthibhiḥ ..
puruṣairdevadeveśa etanme vaktumarhasi .. 7.1.167.70 ..
16.167.d:
.. देव्युवाच ..
कदा पूजा प्रकर्तव्या भूतमातुः सुखार्थिभिः ..
पुरुषैर्देवदेवेश एतन्मे वक्तुमर्हसि .. 7.1.167.70 ..
16.167.m: The goddess said: / When should the worship of the Mother of Spirits be performed by men / desiring happiness, O Lord of the gods of gods? You ought to tell me this. // 70

16.167.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
sarvatraiṣā bhagavatī bālānāṃ hitakāriṇī ..
nāmabhedaiḥ kālabhedaiḥ kriyābhedaiśca pūjyate ..71..
16.167.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
सर्वत्रैषा भगवती बालानां हितकारिणी ..
नामभेदैः कालभेदैः क्रियाभेदैश्च पूज्यते ..71..
16.167.m: Īśvara said: / Everywhere this Blessed Goddess, who brings welfare to children, / is worshipped under diverse names, at different times, and with varied rituals. // 71

16.167.s:
pratipatprabhṛti vaiśākhe yāvaccaturdaśītithiḥ ..
tāvatpūjā prakartavyā preraṇīprekṣaṇīyakaiḥ .. 72 ..
16.167.d:
प्रतिपत्प्रभृति वैशाखे यावच्चतुर्दशीतिथिः ..
तावत्पूजा प्रकर्तव्या प्रेरणीप्रेक्षणीयकैः .. 72 ..
16.167.m: From the first day onwards in the month of Vaiśākha until the fourteenth lunar day, / worship should be performed for that long with pantomimes and spectacles. // 72

16.167.s:
bhagnāmapi gatāṃ caināṃ jarattarutale sthitām ..
secayiṣyaṃti ye bhaktyā jalasaṃpūrṇagaṃḍukaiḥ .. 73 ..
16.167.d:
भग्नामपि गतां चैनां जरत्तरुतले स्थिताम् ..
सेचयिष्यंति ये भक्त्या जलसंपूर्णगंडुकैः .. 73 ..
16.167.m: And who with devotion sprinkle with pots full of water this [goddess], / even if broken, who stands at the foot of an old tree, // 73

16.167.s:
grīvāsūtrakasindūraiḥ puṣpairdhūpaistathārcayet..
tatra siddhavaṭaḥ pūjyaḥ śākhāṃ cāsya vinikṣipet.. 74 ..
16.167.d:
ग्रीवासूत्रकसिन्दूरैः पुष्पैर्धूपैस्तथार्चयेत्..
तत्र सिद्धवटः पूज्यः शाखां चास्य विनिक्षिपेत्.. 74 ..
16.167.m: and worships her with neck-threads, red lead, flowers, and incense; / there the sacred fig tree must be worshipped, and one should cast down its branch. // 74

16.167.s:
pūjitāṃ tāṃ narairyatnādavalokya śubhepsubhiḥ ..
bhojayetkṣiprāsaṃyāvakṛśarāpūpapāyasaiḥ ..75..
16.167.d:
पूजितां तां नरैर्यत्नादवलोक्य शुभेप्सुभिः ..
भोजयेत्क्षिप्रासंयावकृशरापूपपायसैः ..75..
16.167.m: Having beheld her worshipped with effort by men desiring good fortune, / one should feed [her] with porridge, barley cakes, khicḍī, sweet pastries, and milk-rice. // 75

16.167.s:
evaṃ vidhiṃ yaḥ kurute puruṣo bhaktibhāvataḥ ..
sa putrapaśuvṛddhiṃ ca śarīrārogyamāpnuyāt ..76..
16.167.d:
एवं विधिं यः कुरुते पुरुषो भक्तिभावतः ..
स पुत्रपशुवृद्धिं च शरीरारोग्यमाप्नुयात् ..76..
16.167.m: A man who performs the rite in this way with a spirit of devotion / obtains an increase of sons and cattle, and bodily health. // 76

16.167.s:
na śākinyo gṛhe tasya na piśācā na rākṣasāḥ ..
pīḍāṃ kurvanti śiśavo yānti vṛddhimanāmayām .. 77 ..
16.167.d:
न शाकिन्यो गृहे तस्य न पिशाचा न राक्षसाः ..
पीडां कुर्वन्ति शिशवो यान्ति वृद्धिमनामयाम् .. 77 ..
16.167.m: In his house, neither śākinīs, nor piśācas, nor rākṣasas / cause affliction; his children attain growth free from sickness. // 77

16.167.s:
atha devi pravakṣyāmi pratipatprabhṛti kramāt ..
yathotsavo naraiḥ kāryaḥ preraṇīprekṣaṇīyakaiḥ ..78..
16.167.d:
अथ देवि प्रवक्ष्यामि प्रतिपत्प्रभृति क्रमात् ..
यथोत्सवो नरैः कार्यः प्रेरणीप्रेक्षणीयकैः ..78..
16.167.m: Now, O goddess, I shall explain in proper order from the first day onwards / how the festival is to be celebrated by men with pantomimes and spectacles. // 78

16.167.s:
vikarmaphalanirddeśaiḥ pākhaṃḍānāṃ viṭaṃbanaiḥ ..
pradarśyate hāsyaparairnarairadbhutaceṣṭitaiḥ .. 79 ..
16.167.d:
विकर्मफलनिर्द्देशैः पाखंडानां विटंबनैः ..
प्रदर्श्यते हास्यपरैर्नरैरद्भुतचेष्टितैः .. 79 ..
16.167.m: By pointing out the fruits of wicked deeds, through satires of heretics, / it is shown by men intent on humor with astonishing antics: // 79

16.167.s:
pañcamyāṃ tu viśeṣeṇa rātrau kolāhalaḥ śubhe ..
jāgaraṃ tatra kurvīta devīṃ pūjya prayatnataḥ .. 7.1.167.80 ..
16.167.d:
पञ्चम्यां तु विशेषेण रात्रौ कोलाहलः शुभे ..
जागरं तत्र कुर्वीत देवीं पूज्य प्रयत्नतः .. 7.1.167.80 ..
16.167.m: Especially on the fifth [day], O fair one, there is uproar at night; / one should keep vigil then, having carefully worshipped the Goddess. // 80

16.167.s:
viśvasya dhanalobhena svādhyāyo nihataḥ patiḥ..
āropyamāṇaṃ śūlāgramenaṃ paśyata bho janāḥ..81..
16.167.d:
विश्वस्य धनलोभेन स्वाध्यायो निहतः पतिः..
आरोप्यमाणं शूलाग्रमेनं पश्यत भो जनाः..81..
16.167.m: 'Having gained trust, the master who recited scripture was slain out of greed for wealth! / Behold this man being mounted onto the tip of a stake, O people! // 81

16.167.s:
dṛṣṭo bhavadbhirduṣṭaḥ sa paradārāvamarśakaḥ ..
chittvā hastau ca khaḍgena kharārūḍhastu gacchati .. 82 ..
16.167.d:
दृष्टो भवद्भिर्दुष्टः स परदारावमर्शकः ..
छित्त्वा हस्तौ च खड्गेन खरारूढस्तु गच्छति .. 82 ..
16.167.m: Have you seen that wicked violator of another's wife? / His two hands having been cut off with a sword, mounted on a donkey he goes! // 82

16.167.s:
śīrṇaścaivāsipatreṇa asyābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ ..
sukhāsana samārūḍhaḥ sukṛtī yātyasau sukham .. 83 ..
16.167.d:
शीर्णश्चैवासिपत्रेण अस्याभरणभूषितः ..
सुखासन समारूढः सुकृती यात्यसौ सुखम् .. 83 ..
16.167.m: And the one mangled in the sword-leafed forest, [now] adorned with ornaments, / seated upon an easy palanquin—that virtuous man goes happily!' // 83

16.167.s:
he janāḥ kiṃ na paśyadhvaṃ svāmidrohakaraṃ param ..
karapatrairvidāryaṃtamucchalacchoṇitāntaram .. 84 ..
16.167.d:
हे जनाः किं न पश्यध्वं स्वामिद्रोहकरं परम् ..
करपत्रैर्विदार्यंतमुच्छलच्छोणितान्तरम् .. 84 ..
16.167.m: 'O people, do you not see that foremost betrayer of his master / being torn apart with saws, his insides gushing blood? // 84

16.167.s:
cauraḥ kilāyaṃ saṃprāptaḥ sarvodvegakaraḥ paraḥ ..
daṃḍaprahārābhihato nīyate daṃḍapāśakaiḥ .. 85 ..
16.167.d:
चौरः किलायं संप्राप्तः सर्वोद्वेगकरः परः ..
दंडप्रहाराभिहतो नीयते दंडपाशकैः .. 85 ..
16.167.m: This thief has indeed been caught, the great agitator of all! / Struck with blows of a staff, he is led away by the wardens' nooses. // 85

16.167.s:
prekṣakaiśceṣṭitaḥ śaśvadāraṭanvividhaiḥ svaraiḥ ..
saṃyamya nīyate hantuṃ lajjito'dhomukho janāḥ .. 86 ..
16.167.d:
प्रेक्षकैश्चेष्टितः शश्वदारटन्विविधैः स्वरैः ..
संयम्य नीयते हन्तुं लज्जितोऽधोमुखो जनाः .. 86 ..
16.167.m: Surrounded by spectators, howling incessantly with diverse cries, / bound and led to be killed, he hangs his head in shame, O people!' // 86

16.167.s:
sitakeśaṃ sitaśmaśruṃ sitāṃbaradharadhvajam ..
viṭaṃkādyaiśca ceṭībhirhanyamānaṃ na paśyathi ..87..
16.167.d:
सितकेशं सितश्मश्रुं सितांबरधरध्वजम् ..
विटंकाद्यैश्च चेटीभिर्हन्यमानं न पश्यथि ..87..
16.167.m: 'Do you not see him with white hair, white beard, clad in white clothes and banner, / being beaten with cornices and the like by slave-girls? // 87

16.167.s:
gṛhānniṣkrāmya māṃ raṃḍāṃ gṛhaṃ nītvā'karodratim ..
kasmādasau na kurute mūḍho bharaṇapoṣaṇam .. 88 ..
16.167.d:
गृहान्निष्क्राम्य मां रंडां गृहं नीत्वाऽकरोद्रतिम् ..
कस्मादसौ न कुरुते मूढो भरणपोषणम् .. 88 ..
16.167.m: Taking me, a widow, out of the house and bringing me to his home, he had intercourse with me! / Why does this fool not provide maintenance and food?' // 88

16.167.s:
bhairavābharaṇo netā sadā ghūrṇitalocanaḥ ..
pravṛttataṃdravanmūḍho vadhyaścāsāvitastataḥ ..89..
16.167.d:
भैरवाभरणो नेता सदा घूर्णितलोचनः ..
प्रवृत्ततंद्रवन्मूढो वध्यश्चासावितस्ततः ..89..
16.167.m: 'Wearing terrible ornaments, the ringleader, his eyes constantly rolling, / looking foolish as if overtaken by lethargy, is to be executed here and there!' // 89

16.167.s:
nirvedeko'sya hṛdaye dhanakṣetrādisaṃbhavaḥ ..
gṛhītaṃ yadanenādya bālenāpi mahāvratam ..
raktākṣaṃ kākakṛṣṇāṃgaṃ satvaraṃ kiṃ na paśyathi .. 7.1.167.90 ..
16.167.d:
निर्वेदेकोऽस्य हृदये धनक्षेत्रादिसंभवः ..
गृहीतं यदनेनाद्य बालेनापि महाव्रतम् ..
रक्ताक्षं काककृष्णांगं सत्वरं किं न पश्यथि .. 7.1.167.90 ..
16.167.m: 'What disillusionment in his heart arose from wealth, field, and the like, / that this great vow has been taken today even by this boy? / Why do you not quickly look at him, with red eyes and a body black as a crow?' // 90

16.167.s:
tarukoṭaragānbaddhvā anyāñchṛṃkhalayā tathā ..
śaraughaiḥ kāṣṭhakaiścaiva bahubhiḥ śakalīkṛtān .. 91 ..
16.167.d:
तरुकोटरगान्बद्ध्वा अन्याञ्छृंखलया तथा ..
शरौघैः काष्ठकैश्चैव बहुभिः शकलीकृतान् .. 91 ..
16.167.m: Having bound those residing in tree hollows, and others likewise with chains, / cut to pieces with heaps of arrows and sticks, // 91

16.167.s: vimuktahakkāhuṃkārā nsuprahārānnirīkṣata .. 92 ..
16.167.d: विमुक्तहक्काहुंकारा न्सुप्रहारान्निरीक्षत .. 92 ..
16.167.m: emitting yells and growls—behold the heavy blows! // 92

16.167.s:
imāṃ kṛṣṇārdhavadanāṃ grahīṣyasi durātmikām ..
vimuktakeśāṃ nṛtyantīṃ paśyadhvaṃ yoginīmiva .. 93 ..
16.167.d:
इमां कृष्णार्धवदनां ग्रहीष्यसि दुरात्मिकाम् ..
विमुक्तकेशां नृत्यन्तीं पश्यध्वं योगिनीमिव .. 93 ..
16.167.m: 'Will you seize this evil-souled woman whose face is half-black? / Behold her dancing with dishevelled hair, like a yoginī!' // 93

16.167.s:
gambhīra nūpuradhvānapravṛddhoddhatatāṃḍavā ..
unmattanetracaraṇā yātyeṣā ḍimbhamaṇḍalī .. 94 ..
16.167.d:
गम्भीर नूपुरध्वानप्रवृद्धोद्धततांडवा ..
उन्मत्तनेत्रचरणा यात्येषा डिम्भमण्डली .. 94 ..
16.167.m: With a wild, frantic dance increasing to the deep sound of anklets, / with crazed eyes and feet, this troop of children moves along. // 94

16.167.s:
kaṭītaṭasthapiṭikollasatkaṃbaladhāriṇī ..
aṭate naṭatī hyurvī paritaśca gṛhādgṛham .. 95 ..
16.167.d:
कटीतटस्थपिटिकोल्लसत्कंबलधारिणी ..
अटते नटती ह्युर्वी परितश्च गृहाद्गृहम् .. 95 ..
16.167.m: Wearing a basket hung at the hips and a shining blanket, / a dancing actress indeed roams all around the earth from house to house. // 95

16.167.s:
ityevamādibhirnityaṃ preraṇīprekṣaṇīyakaiḥ ..
prerayettānmahānitthaṃ putrabhrātṛsuhṛdvṛtaḥ .. 96 ..
16.167.d:
इत्येवमादिभिर्नित्यं प्रेरणीप्रेक्षणीयकैः ..
प्रेरयेत्तान्महानित्थं पुत्रभ्रातृसुहृद्वृतः .. 96 ..
16.167.m: With such pantomimes and spectacles daily, / the great man, surrounded by sons, brothers, and friends, should encourage them thus. // 96

16.167.s:
ekādaśyāṃ navamyāṃ vā dīpaṃ prajvālya kuṇḍakam ..
mukhabiṃbāni tatraiva lepadārukṛtāni vai .. 97 ..
16.167.d:
एकादश्यां नवम्यां वा दीपं प्रज्वाल्य कुण्डकम् ..
मुखबिंबानि तत्रैव लेपदारुकृतानि वै .. 97 ..
16.167.m: On the eleventh or the ninth [day], having lit a lamp in a hollow basin, / right there [one should make] masks fashioned of plaster and wood; // 97

16.167.s:
vicitrāṇi mahārhāṇi raudraśāntāni kārayet ..
mātṛṇāṃ caṇḍikādīnāṃ rākṣasānāṃ tathaiva ca .. 98 ..
16.167.d:
विचित्राणि महार्हाणि रौद्रशान्तानि कारयेत् ..
मातृणां चण्डिकादीनां राक्षसानां तथैव च .. 98 ..
16.167.m: one should have diverse, highly valuable, terrible, and peaceful masks made: / of the Mothers, Caṇḍikā and others, and likewise of rākṣasas, // 98

16.167.s:
bhūtapretapiśācānāṃ śākinīnāṃ tathaiva ca ..
mukhāni kārayettatra hāvabhāvakṛtāni ca .. 99 ..
16.167.d:
भूतप्रेतपिशाचानां शाकिनीनां तथैव च ..
मुखानि कारयेत्तत्र हावभावकृतानि च .. 99 ..
16.167.m: and of bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, and likewise of śākinīs; / one should have faces made there displaying various moods and emotions. // 99

16.167.s:
rakṣibhirbahubhirguptaṃ tirya gdhvanipuraḥsaram ..
amāvāsyāṃ mahādevi kṣipetpūjākramairnaraḥ .. 7.1.167.100 ..
16.167.d:
रक्षिभिर्बहुभिर्गुप्तं तिर्य ग्ध्वनिपुरःसरम् ..
अमावास्यां महादेवि क्षिपेत्पूजाक्रमैर्नरः .. 7.1.167.100 ..
16.167.m: Guarded by many guards, preceded by whistling and roaring sounds, / on the new moon day, O Great Goddess, a man should offer it in the order of worship. // 100

16.167.s:
tataḥ pradoṣasamaye yatra devī janairvṛtā ..
tatra gacchenmahārāvaiḥ phetkārā kulakīrtanaiḥ .. 101 ..
16.167.d:
ततः प्रदोषसमये यत्र देवी जनैर्वृता ..
तत्र गच्छेन्महारावैः फेत्कारा कुलकीर्तनैः .. 101 ..
16.167.m: Then, at the time of dusk, where the Goddess is surrounded by the people, / one should go there with great shouts, chanting filled with shrieks. // 101

16.167.s:
vīracaryāvidhānena nagare bhrāmayenniśi ..
vīracaryā sa kathito dīpaḥ sarvārthasādhakaḥ .. 102 ..
16.167.d:
वीरचर्याविधानेन नगरे भ्रामयेन्निशि ..
वीरचर्या स कथितो दीपः सर्वार्थसाधकः .. 102 ..
16.167.m: According to the rite of the heroes' practice, one should carry it around the city at night; / that lamp, which accomplishes all purposes, is called the 'heroes' practice'. // 102

16.167.s:
nityaṃ niṣkrāmayeddīpaṃ yāva tpañcadaśī tithiḥ ..
pañcadaśyāṃ prakurvīta bhūtamāturmahotsavam ..
tasya gṛheśvaraṃ yāvadgṛhe vighnaṃ na jāyate .. 103 ..
16.167.d:
नित्यं निष्क्रामयेद्दीपं याव त्पञ्चदशी तिथिः ..
पञ्चदश्यां प्रकुर्वीत भूतमातुर्महोत्सवम् ..
तस्य गृहेश्वरं यावद्गृहे विघ्नं न जायते .. 103 ..
16.167.m: Daily he should bring out the lamp until the fifteenth lunar day; / on the fifteenth he should celebrate the grand festival of the Mother of Spirits; / as long as he lives as master in that house, no obstacle will arise in the home. // 103

16.167.s:
atha kālāntare'tīte bhūtamātuḥ śarīrataḥ ..
jātāḥ prasvedabindubhyaḥ piśācāḥ pañcakoṭayaḥ .. 104 ..
16.167.d:
अथ कालान्तरेऽतीते भूतमातुः शरीरतः ..
जाताः प्रस्वेदबिन्दुभ्यः पिशाचाः पञ्चकोटयः .. 104 ..
16.167.m: Then, after a period of time had passed, from the body of the Mother of spirits (Bhūtamātṛ), / from drops of sweat, fifty million piśācas were born. (104)

16.167.s:
sarve te krūravadanā jihvājvālākṛśodarāḥ ..
pāṇipātrāḥ piśācāste nisṛṣṭabalibhojanāḥ .. 105 ..
16.167.d:
सर्वे ते क्रूरवदना जिह्वाज्वालाकृशोदराः ..
पाणिपात्राः पिशाचास्ते निसृष्टबलिभोजनाः .. 105 ..
16.167.m: They all had cruel faces, their tongues like flames, their bellies emaciated; / using their hands as bowls, those piśācas fed upon cast-off offerings. (105)

16.167.s:
dhamanīsaṃtatāḥ śuṣkāḥ śmaśrulāścarmavāsasaḥ ..
ulūkhalairābharaṇaiḥ śūrpacchatrāsanāṃbarāḥ .. 106 ..
16.167.d:
धमनीसंतताः शुष्काः श्मश्रुलाश्चर्मवाससः ..
उलूखलैराभरणैः शूर्पच्छत्रासनांबराः .. 106 ..
16.167.m: Covered with veins, withered, bearded, clad in hides, / having wooden mortars as ornaments, with winnowing baskets for umbrellas, seats, and garments, (106)

16.167.s:
naktaṃ jvalitakeśāḍhyā aṃgārānudgiraṃti vai ..
aṃgārakāḥ piśācāste mātṛmārgānusāriṇaḥ .. 107 ..
16.167.d:
नक्तं ज्वलितकेशाढ्या अंगारानुद्गिरंति वै ..
अंगारकाः पिशाचास्ते मातृमार्गानुसारिणः .. 107 ..
16.167.m: having burning hair at night, indeed spitting out burning coals— / those coal-like piśācas followed the way of the Mother. (107)

16.167.s:
ākarṇadāritāsyāśca laṃbabhrūsthūlanāsikāḥ ..
balāḍhyāste piśācā vai sūtikāgṛhavāsinaḥ .. 108 ..
16.167.d:
आकर्णदारितास्याश्च लंबभ्रूस्थूलनासिकाः ..
बलाढ्यास्ते पिशाचा वै सूतिकागृहवासिनः .. 108 ..
16.167.m: With mouths torn open to the ears, drooping brows, and thick noses, / those mighty piśācas indeed dwelt in lying-in chambers. (108)

16.167.s:
pṛṣṭhataḥ pāṇipādāśca pṛṣṭhagā vātaraṃhasā ..
viṣādanāḥ piśācāste saṃgrāme piśitāśanāḥ .. .. 109 ..
16.167.d:
पृष्ठतः पाणिपादाश्च पृष्ठगा वातरंहसा ..
विषादनाः पिशाचास्ते संग्रामे पिशिताशनाः .. .. 109 ..
16.167.m: Having their hands and feet backward, moving backward with the swiftness of the wind, / terrifying, those piśācas fed on raw flesh in battle. (109)

16.167.s:
evaṃvidhānpiśācāṃstu dṛṣṭvā dīnānukampayā ..
tebhyo'hamavadaṃ kiñcitkāruṇyādalpacetasām .. 7.1.167.110 ..
16.167.d:
एवंविधान्पिशाचांस्तु दृष्ट्वा दीनानुकम्पया ..
तेभ्योऽहमवदं किञ्चित्कारुण्यादल्पचेतसाम् .. 7.1.167.110 ..
16.167.m: Seeing such piśācas, out of compassion for the wretched, / out of mercy I spoke a little to those feeble-minded beings: (110)

16.167.s:
antardhānaṃ prajādehe kāmarūpitvameva ca ..
ubhayoḥ saṃdhyayoścāraṃ sthānānyājīvitaṃ tathā .. 111 ..
16.167.d:
अन्तर्धानं प्रजादेहे कामरूपित्वमेव च ..
उभयोः संध्ययोश्चारं स्थानान्याजीवितं तथा .. 111 ..
16.167.m: ‘Invisibility within the bodies of creatures, the power to change shape at will, / wandering at both twilights, your dwelling places, and likewise your livelihood; (111)

16.167.s:
gṛhāṇi yāni nagnāni śūnyānyāyatanāni ca ..
vidhvastāni ca yāni syū racanāroṣitāni ca.. 112 ..
16.167.d:
गृहाणि यानि नग्नानि शून्यान्यायतनानि च ..
विध्वस्तानि च यानि स्यू रचनारोषितानि च.. 112 ..
16.167.m: houses that are bare, empty temples, / and those that are ruined and stripped of decoration, (112)

16.167.s:
rājamārgoparathyāśca catvarāṇi trikāṇi ca ..
dvārāṇyaṭṭālakāṃścaiva nirgamānsaṃkramāṃstathā .. .. 113 ..
16.167.d:
राजमार्गोपरथ्याश्च चत्वराणि त्रिकाणि च ..
द्वाराण्यट्टालकांश्चैव निर्गमान्संक्रमांस्तथा .. .. 113 ..
16.167.m: highways, side streets, crossroads, and junctions of three roads, / gates, watchtowers, exits, and causeways, (113)

16.167.s:
patho nadīśca tīrthāni caityavṛkṣānmahāpathān ..
sthānāni tu piśācānāṃ nivāsāyādadāṃ priye .. 114 ..
16.167.d:
पथो नदीश्च तीर्थानि चैत्यवृक्षान्महापथान् ..
स्थानानि तु पिशाचानां निवासायाददां प्रिये .. 114 ..
16.167.m: paths, rivers, sacred fords, sacred caitya trees, and great roads— / these places I have given as dwellings for the piśācas, O dear one. (114)

16.167.s:
adhārmikā janāsteṣāmā jīvo vihitaḥ purā ..
varṇāśramācārahīnāḥ kāruśilpijanāstathā .. 115 ..
16.167.d:
अधार्मिका जनास्तेषामा जीवो विहितः पुरा ..
वर्णाश्रमाचारहीनाः कारुशिल्पिजनास्तथा .. 115 ..
16.167.m: Unrighteous people were formerly ordained as their livelihood, / along with those devoid of the conduct of the classes and life-stages, as well as artisans and craftsmen, (115)

16.167.s:
anutāpāśca sādhūnāṃ caurā viśvāsaghātinaḥ ..
etairanyaiśca bahubhiranyāyopārjitairdhanaiḥ .. 116 ..
16.167.d:
अनुतापाश्च साधूनां चौरा विश्वासघातिनः ..
एतैरन्यैश्च बहुभिरन्यायोपार्जितैर्धनैः .. 116 ..
16.167.m: those who cause remorse to good people, thieves, and betrayers of trust. / When any rites are undertaken with wealth unjustly acquired (116)

16.167.s:
ārabhyate kriyā yāstu piśācāstatra devatāḥ ..
madhumāsadine dadhnā tilacūrṇasurāsavaiḥ .. 117 ..
16.167.d:
आरभ्यते क्रिया यास्तु पिशाचास्तत्र देवताः ..
मधुमासदिने दध्ना तिलचूर्णसुरासवैः .. 117 ..
16.167.m: by these and many others, the piśācas are the deities there. / On a day in the spring month, with curd, sesame powder, and intoxicating liquors, (117)

16.167.s:
pūpairhāridrakṛśaraistilairikṣuguḍaudanaiḥ ..
kṛṣṇāni caiva vāsāṃsi dhūmrāḥ sumanasastathā .. 118 ..
16.167.d:
पूपैर्हारिद्रकृशरैस्तिलैरिक्षुगुडौदनैः ..
कृष्णानि चैव वासांसि धूम्राः सुमनसस्तथा .. 118 ..
16.167.m: with cakes, turmeric-infused khichdi, sesame seeds, sugarcane, molasses, and boiled rice, / and with black garments and smoky-colored flowers, (118)

16.167.s:
sarvabhūtapiśācānāṃ kṛtā devī mayā śubhā ..
evaṃvidhā bhūtamātā sarvabhūtagaṇairvṛtā .. 119 ..
16.167.d:
सर्वभूतपिशाचानां कृता देवी मया शुभा ..
एवंविधा भूतमाता सर्वभूतगणैर्वृता .. 119 ..
16.167.m: the auspicious goddess was made by me for all bhūtas and piśācas.’ / Such is the Mother of spirits, surrounded by all the host of bhūtas. (119)

16.167.s:
prabhāse saṃsthitā devī samudrāduttareṇa tu ..
ya etāṃ veda vai devyā utpattiṃ pāpanāśinīm .. 7.1.167.120 ..
16.167.d:
प्रभासे संस्थिता देवी समुद्रादुत्तरेण तु ..
य एतां वेद वै देव्या उत्पत्तिं पापनाशिनीम् .. 7.1.167.120 ..
16.167.m: The goddess is situated in Prabhāsa, to the north of the ocean. / Whoever knows this origin of the goddess, which destroys sin, (120)

16.167.s:
kutsitā saṃtati stasya na bhavecca kadācana ..
bhūtapretapiśācānāṃ na doṣaiḥ paribhūyate .. 121 ..
16.167.d:
कुत्सिता संतति स्तस्य न भवेच्च कदाचन ..
भूतप्रेतपिशाचानां न दोषैः परिभूयते .. 121 ..
16.167.m: his lineage shall never become vile, / nor is he overcome by the afflictions of bhūtas, pretas, and piśācas. (121)

16.167.s:
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ sarvasaubhāgyasaṃyutaḥ ..
sarvānkāmānavāpnoti nārīhṛdayanaṃdanaḥ .. 122 ..
16.167.d:
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तः सर्वसौभाग्यसंयुतः ..
सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति नारीहृदयनंदनः .. 122 ..
16.167.m: Freed from all sin, endowed with all good fortune, / he attains all desires, bringing joy to the hearts of women. (122)

16.167.s:
ye mānayaṃti nijahāsakalairvilāsaiḥ saṃsevayā abhayadā bhavabhūtamātām ..
te bhrātṛbhṛtyasutabaṃdhujanairyutāśca sarvopasarga rahitāḥ sukhino bhavanti .. 123 ..
16.167.d:
ये मानयंति निजहासकलैर्विलासैः संसेवया अभयदा भवभूतमाताम् ..
